subject: It is in these extraordinary moments that America's character is revealed

body:
Your support helps ensure that our progress continues toward that more perfect union we all seek, no matter how challenging the path.
| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106767467/542576107/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImY4ZDFlODBkLTU2MjUtZjAxMS04YjNkLTYwNDViZGVkOGNjYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=B5jp6QE_jQXetqiPvplSKtL4531PyERC8jCZc89P9qE=&emci=dd835291-2d21-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=f8d1e80d-5625-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=8431045)

Peter, we must confront the fact that our great country is going through a generational regression. Misinformation, disinformation, and injustice loom over society like a dark cloud. The rule of law and fundamental fairness are at risk. Governing norms have been needlessly cast aside. Compassion in our government is in short supply. **In this time of maximum danger to our country, all who love America most dearly must stand up and speak out for the principles that, at our best, define the nation.** As I reflect on our current challenges, I am reminded of a critical moment in a turbulent era of our nation's history: On June 11, 1963, the Deputy Attorney General, Nicholas Katzenbach, peacefully escorted James Hood and my late sister-in-law Vivian Malone onto campus as they integrated the University of Alabama, past Governor Wallace's infamous blockade. That evening, President Kennedy addressed the American people not merely about a political disagreement, but about a profound moral reckoning for our republic. Every single word rang with conviction and moral clarity, making the case and pointing the way toward what would become the signature achievements of the Civil Rights Era and the foundation of modern America. Today, our current moment presents both possibility and peril for the fundamental freedoms and pro-democracy principles we hold dear. **It is in these extraordinary moments — these complex and contradictory chapters in the life of our nation — and through the work of ordinary yet extraordinary people that America's character is revealed, and our future determined.** Right now, the progress we have made as a nation — long sought and long fought for — is being dismantled right before our very eyes. We see it in House Republicans passing the extreme SAVE Act, which could disenfranchise millions of Americans. We see it in North Carolina, where Republican Jefferson Griffin is attempting to steal a seat on that state's highest court. We see it in relentless GOP efforts to gerrymander districts across the country, silencing the voices of millions. But make no mistake: there is still reason for hope. Just look at Wisconsin, where ordinary yet extraordinary people — who suffered under years of illegitimate minority rule amid ruthless gerrymandering — kept pressing forward for a truly representative democracy. At the NDRC, we’ve been proud to fight by their side. After years of steadfast work, the people of Wisconsin finally won a pro-democracy majority on the state supreme court that helped deliver fair maps — which meant a fair chance for all Wisconsinites to be heard. And earlier this month, we were proud to work alongside them as they protected that majority by electing Justice Susan Crawford to the Wisconsin Supreme Court. Their example is a testament to what's possible when we organize and fight together. **So today, I'm asking you directly: please stay engaged in this critical fight. [**Your support of the NDRC before our end-of-month deadline will power the hard, and absolutely necessary work of defending our democracy — to protect fair maps, combat ongoing gerrymandering, and prepare for the redistricting battles that lie ahead.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106767468/542576108/1925646595?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_AGAprilEOMAppeal_email_20250429-NDRC-Tier1-AGAprilEOMAppeal_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250429-NDRC-Tier1-AGAprilEOMAppeal_&utm_campaign=AGAprilEOMAppeal&amount=30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImY4ZDFlODBkLTU2MjUtZjAxMS04YjNkLTYwNDViZGVkOGNjYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=B5jp6QE_jQXetqiPvplSKtL4531PyERC8jCZc89P9qE=)** Thank you, Eric H. This case isn't new. A three-judge panel found that Alabama's maps violated the VRA in 2022, and the Supreme Court agreed in 2023. Alabama used the court-mandated nonpartisan map in 2024, then turned right around to try and put their gerrymandered, suppressive map back in place for 2026.
When voters are silenced and votes are suppressed anywhere our democracy is harmed everywhere. Pitch in $25 or more right now to spread the word about this case and fight for fair maps nationwide >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2?am=25.00&contactdata=pFNdZWKser4nwhSRkLpmkLsghe9gLZDruJpI+N7gQSvsqHJSOS7fKWqF+GP9zQcaxddCL3GIuPZR0sf/v9pngHMc4Zl+qLT+RxosnUervxc=]
AP: Alabama’s congressional map at stake in federal Voting Rights Act trial [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2?am=20.00&contactdata=pFNdZWKser4nwhSRkLpmkLsghe9gLZDruJpI+N7gQSvsqHJSOS7fKWqF+GP9zQcaxddCL3GIuPZR0sf/v9pngHMc4Zl+qLT+RxosnUervxc=]
Folks,
Alabama’s congressional map is at stake in a federal trial that wil decide if the state will keep the new court-created district that led to the election of a second Black representative. From the AP:
" A three-judge panel will decide whether congressional lines drawn by state lawmakers diluted the voting power of Black residents. The same panel already ruled against Alabama in pre-trial decisions that reshaped the 2nd Congressional District before Rep. Shomari Figures won election in November, giving Alabama two Black representatives in its delegation for the first time in history. "
The state of Alabama is seeking to reinstate the maps created by the suppressive state legislature. This case began in 2021 when Black voters and civil rights groups filed lawsuits over Alabama’s state-drawn congressional map they said disenfranchised Black voters.
Team, we have to make sure voters everywhere know about this case to protect fair maps in court. Please pitch in $25 or whatever you can to help us make every vote count, either at the ballot box or in court >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2?am=25.00&contactdata=pFNdZWKser4nwhSRkLpmkLsghe9gLZDruJpI+N7gQSvsqHJSOS7fKWqF+GP9zQcaxddCL3GIuPZR0sf/v9pngHMc4Zl+qLT+RxosnUervxc=]

Defenders of voting rights believe they can show a level of continuing, intentional discrimination that should once again make Alabama subject to the preclearance requirement of the 1965 Voting Rights Act.
Deuel Ross, an attorney with the NAACP Legal Defense Fund who represents the plaintiffs seeking to protect the current map, said " This is sort of exactly the thing that Alabama and other states did before the Voting Rights Act — a court would find that there was some sort of discrimination in the way in which they were drawing maps or registering voters and the state would respond by essentially doing the same thing over again, but dressing it up in a slightly different outfit ".
Attacks like this on what remains of the Voting Rights Act are going to get worse over the next few years. As voter suppression laws become increasingly targeted and gerrymandering more oppressive , our work to defend the right to vote must become smarter, stronger, and more accessible to everyone.
We can't do this alone. | It was a pleasure to help host Wofford’s newest political series, “Candid Conversations” with Trey Gowdy, political commentator on Fox and former Congressman for SC-04 alongside Bakari Sellers, political commentator for CNN and former SC Representative for HD 90, and our moderator Billy Webster, wofford professor and former White House aid. Open dialogue is integral to our democracy. Open dialogue can help us reach across our differences to counter polarization. I am proud to be a part of a series that challenges our current administration’s norms. Speaking of open dialogue.... # Due Process is integral to our democracy
---
| | | | [|
---](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=41c8565588&e=edbde6c9b1)
| In the wake of the case against Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a larger conversation about the rule of law and state of our country has emerged. The ongoing legal saga of a wrongly deported immigrant from El Salvador has created a situation where it seems that President Trump can deny due process to anyone — not just immigrants living in the U.S. without legal status.
Everyone in the U.S., including those without legal status, have constitutional rights to due process under the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments. Isn’t William Timmons an attorney? What does he have to say about this?
“Due process is the language of a constitutional democracy, and so we have to speak that language so people can understand other people’s situations,” Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) said in an interview. “And I do believe that if we don’t stand up for the due process rights of non-citizens, they will quickly trample the due process rights of citizens.”
I had the honor of interviewing David Blanton, former pastor and DOJ accredited legal representative for immigrants in the Upstate, for my episode tomorrow with Frogmore Stew. Our conversation dives into this very topic: What can we do to support our neighbors locally and defend due process? Make sure to Tune in **Every Wednesday** as I join the crew from [**Frogmore Stew - SC’s pop-politics podcast**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=1e10295550&e=edbde6c9b1) \- as their weekly contributor from the Upstate.

| | | | | | | | | | | | [**Private school vouchers to exclude disability protections**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=c40fc83163&e=edbde6c9b1)**-**[**Contact your Senator TODAY**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=29e6e4ef43&e=edbde6c9b1) State lawmakers have been pushing bill ([Senate Bill 62](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=f84ac790b7&e=edbde6c9b1)) that would send public funds to private K-12 schools, including religious schools. They are doing this despite the State Supreme Court telling the state in September that a nearly identical program violated the state constitution. Senate Majority Leader Shane Massey told reporters he intends to get S. 62 passed **TODAY**. The current version of the bill allows voucher recipient schools to ignore Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), which ordinarily require a school to serve the educational needs of students with disabilities. About [15% of public school students](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=4e196ecff4&e=edbde6c9b1) have an IEP. The latest version of the bill also allows the General Assembly to fund 15,000 vouchers per year, worth $7,500 apiece, either by stealing funds from the state's general fund or by diverting revenue from the South Carolina Education Lottery, which currently funds in-state college scholarships.
---
**190,000+ SC Voters: Check Your Mail!**
In an ongoing effort to maintain the integrity of South Carolina’s statewide voter registration list, [**State Election Commission is sending voter confirmation postcards**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=771c5b3244&e=edbde6c9b1) to 190,000+ who haven't voted since 2020 General Election and not updated their voter info. That you? When it arrives: sign it, date it, and drop it back in the mail within 90 days _(will already be stamped & addressed)_
|

| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | [**House Bill 3645**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=e32aee8b94&e=edbde6c9b1)**\- 12-week paid family leave up for debate** House Bill 3645 is now on the House debate calendar. This bill would give all South Carolina state employees up to 12 weeks of paid family leave. This time is essential for parents to recover from childbirth, bond with a new child, or care for a seriously ill loved one without losing income. Tell your representative to vote yes on H. 3645 by [**clicking WREN’s action link.**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=efea629e3b&e=edbde6c9b1)
[**Contact your legislators**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=4eeb185126&e=edbde6c9b1)**about**[**House Bill 4397**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=9899d78d4f&e=edbde6c9b1)**\- Protect Greenville County Public Schools** South Carolina House Bill 4397 (H. 4397) amends Act 602 of 1992, which governs the [Greenville County School District](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=64e68f41e1&e=edbde6c9b1). Specifically, the bill requires the Greenville County Council to approve the school district's budget. Moms for Liberty is in support of the bill — Greenville's conservative county council would use this power to censor and control what children in the public school system could learn.
| **Subcommittee approves**[**House Bill 3758**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=c84d81081f&e=edbde6c9b1)**\- the school proselytization bill** Last week the House Education and Public Works Committee gave a favorable report on [House Bill 3758](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=838a197e0b&e=edbde6c9b1), which would allow students to deliver religious messages at forums including graduation ceremonies, morning announcements, assemblies, and the start of athletic events. The bill can now be debated on the House floor. Students have the right to pray during free time at school and to participate in before- and after-school religious events and student religious clubs. We oppose efforts to subject public school students to prayer and proselytizing during official school events, a clear violation of the First Amendment’s prohibition on establishment of religion.

# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=8523%2E5257348%2EBrSutQ)
Derek —
We’re 100 days into the Trump administration, and in this short time, he has actively and blatantly violated the law, undermined the U.S. Constitution in countless ways, and attacked the patriotic men and women who serve our country.
Trump has done nothing but act like he is above the law. He’s drunk on power, reckless, and refuses to take accountability for any of the actions he and his administration have done to undermine our democracy.
But Adam is fighting back. He’s doing everything in his power to stop Trump and his administration from lawlessness — from blocking judicial nominations, calling for congressional hearings, and demanding investigations so we can have answers on Trump’s continued abuse of power.

subject: Add your name: Protect Wisconsin’s public schools from Trump’s reckless cuts
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tony for Wisconsin
body:
Our kids and schools deserve better. Join the fight
| Derek,

**Governor Tony Evers just took a major step to defend Wisconsin’s kids and public schools — and he needs your support.**

The Trump Administration is once again attacking public education, threatening to strip more than half a billion dollars in critical federal funding from Wisconsin’s schools. These are funds our schools rely on every day to keep class sizes small, recruit and retain quality educators, support students with special needs, and ensure every child — no matter their background — has access to a high-quality education.

**As a former teacher, principal, and superintendent, Gov. Evers knows firsthand what’s at stake. That’s why Wisconsin has joined a lawsuit to stop the Trump Administration’s unlawful and dangerous attempts to gut funding for our kids, our families, and our future.**

The Trump Administration’s reckless cuts would devastate Wisconsin schools — just to help pay for tax breaks for millionaires and billionaires. Worse yet, they are trying to impose these cuts without Congressional approval, undermining the constitutional checks and balances that protect all of us.

Gov. Evers is standing up for our kids, our public schools, and our democracy. Now he needs all of us to stand with him.

[**_Add your name today to support Gov. Evers’ fight to protect Wisconsin’s kids, families, and schools >>_**](https://go.tonyevers.com/go/2675?t=5&akid=7126%2E1827488%2E0S_e3_) | | [Add Your Name](https://go.tonyevers.com/go/2675?t=7&akid=7126%2E1827488%2E0S_e3_)

Thank you for standing up for Wisconsin’s future.

— Team Evers

name: Ilhan Omar
subject: the American people are paying attention
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20250429-1335-foote&t=1001&akid=1335%2E342411%2ERkhp8P ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter — The
first 100 days of Trump’s second term has been defined by lies, chaos, and
destruction.

Destruction of the rule of law, of checks and balances, and of the entire
Constitutional order that has governed our nation (for better or for
worse) for almost 250 years.

Families and communities are being torn apart as ICE makes arrests and
deportations to stifle free speech without due process. Working class
folks have been left in the lurch as Elon Musk slashes crucial programs
that millions rely on. And everyone has been on edge as Trump’s tariff war
damages the economy and raises the cost of goods.

The situation is dire, but the American people are paying attention.

Polls show that Trump’s approval rating at 100 days is now lower than any
president in at least seven decades.

His approval on issues like the economy and immigration are at all time
lows, and millions of key voters who decided the election last year
already regret their choice.

We must aggressively rally anyone who has been disaffected by Trump’s
failed first 100 days to our movement for democracy and progress.

This is our time and our opportunity,
Peter. People see the damage of Trump’s far-right
agenda, but they need an alternative they can believe in. I know that our
progressive movement can offer a better way forward for our country, but
we need to get the message out there, and that takes resources.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20250429-2-movement.0UZ-2b&refcode=em20250429-1335&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=1335%2E342411%2ERkhp8P ]Peter
— Will you make a contribution of $3 or whatever you can
afford today to the Squad Victory Fund and help us continue to build the
nationwide opposition to Donald Trump? We are gaining ground, which means
now is the time to push even harder, and we can’t do that without you:

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20250429-2-movement.0UZ-2b&refcode=em20250429-1335&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1021&akid=1335%2E342411%2ERkhp8P ]Contribute ››

In solidarity,

Ilhan Omar

subject: BREAKING: My 16th lawsuit against Trump
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ROB BONTA FOR CALIFORNIA ATTORNEY GENERAL 2026 FPPC ID #145642
body:
AmeriCorps volunteers bring out the best in America, California, and our communities.
# [](https://act.robbonta.com/go/3?refcode=em20250429&t=1&akid=1760%2E1088799%2EUNRcGL)
Breaking news:
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-20250429?refcode=em20250429-1760&refcode2=1760_1088799_UNRcGL&akid=1760%2E1088799%2EUNRcGL)
**I just filed my 16th lawsuit against the Trump administration. This time, it’s for dismantling AmeriCorps** , the national volunteer public service agency, by terminating grant funding and slashing its workforce by 85 percent.
**[If you have my back in this new legal fight, rush a contribution to support us →](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-20250429?refcode=em20250429-1760&refcode2=1760_1088799_UNRcGL&akid=1760%2E1088799%2EUNRcGL)**
AmeriCorps supports national and state community service programs by providing opportunities for more than 200,000 Americans to directly serve their communities every year and awarding grants to agencies and organizations that help address critical needs in our communities. In California, AmeriCorps volunteers build affordable housing, clean up our environment, address food insecurity, support veterans, and so much more.
AmeriCorps touched my life in such a meaningful way. When I was fresh out of college and taking my first steps toward my career, I worked with an AmeriCorps program in Connecticut called Leadership, Education & Athletics in Partnership (LEAP) that served children and families in public housing neighborhoods. My time with LEAP inspired me to pursue a career in public service, focus on uplifting my fellow Americans, and tackle some of our biggest domestic challenges like poverty, affordable housing, quality education, and gun violence. It was perhaps my most formative service experience and helped put me on the trajectory to be your Attorney General today.
**AmeriCorps volunteers bring out the best in America and our communities.** It would be a shame to turn away the hundreds of thousands of young people ready and eager to serve their country, and for communities to lose the vital services they provide.
It’s this spirit of focusing on _us and we_ instead of I and me, of helping one another and taking care of our fellow Americans, that President Trump and Elon Musk are attacking with these cuts. Not only that, but _they’re breaking the law to do so_. So once again, I’m taking them to court.
**[My team and I stand prepared to protect AmeriCorps and the services it gives to our communities — will you stand with me by pitching in $5 or more?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-20250429?refcode=em20250429-1760&amount=5&refcode2=1760_1088799_UNRcGL&akid=1760%2E1088799%2EUNRcGL)**

In solidarity,
Rob

name: AOC
subject: Unpredictable things can happen
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Please do not fall for the illusion or the lie that any action is too small. **There is no action too small**.
In fact, when millions of us _do_ tiny things, we _can_ disrupt these systems. I'm not saying that getting in the game is going 100% to change the outcome, but it may, because **we are in an unprecedented time**.
The unprecedented time can mean, of course, many bad things happen — but it can also mean that **unpredictable things can happen, and can even go our way**.
I was elected in the first Trump administration and nobody ever, _ever_ thought that I have a prayer in order to win. I was a waitress. I was challenging the head of a political machine who was supposed to be the next Speaker of the House.
They spent $3 million against me while I was wiping down tables, and we won. Why?
**Because an unpredictable window has opened**.
Do not comply in advance. You try anyway.
We will not be afraid – **because that’s what they want**.
But our movement for real progress will have to push harder than ever these next four years.
[Help us continue the fight with a grassroots contribution today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20250429-2.1BkXne&refcode=em20250429-8723-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=8723%2E2526796%2EayuP0u)

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Our first candidate of the 2026 election cycle is here — and this campaign
is already making headlines because it’s about something bigger: taking on
the political establishment to build a Democratic Party that works for
working people, not millionaires.

Fight for Real Representation in Detroit's 13th District" along with an
image of Donavan. He is smiling with his arms crossed. He wears a navy
suit with a white shirt and a silver tie.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20250429-2-dm?refcode=em20250429-36627&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36627_1203867_NOYzmg&akid=36627%2E1203867%2ENOYzmg ]Headline from The Washington Post reading "Democratic fight over
party's future arrives in a Michigan congressional race." Subhead reads
"Justice Democrats, a group with a record of backing younger, more liberal
challengers against older, more moderate Democratic incumbents, is
endorsing state Rep. Donavan McKinney.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20250429-2-dm?refcode=em20250429-36627&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36627_1203867_NOYzmg&akid=36627%2E1203867%2ENOYzmg ]Headline from The American Prospect reading "The Squad Could Have aa
New Member in 2026", subhead "Justice Democrats endorses Donavan McKinney,
their first endorsement in four years, to challenge multimillionaire Shri
Thanedar for a House seat.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20250429-2-dm?refcode=em20250429-36627&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36627_1203867_NOYzmg&akid=36627%2E1203867%2ENOYzmg ]Headline from Notus reading "Another Black Democrat Lines Up to
Challenge Shri Thanedar With Justice Democrats' Backing". Subhead reads
"The outcome of the 2026 Democratic primaries could determine whether
detroit will return to Black representation in Congress."

This is a big deal, Peter.

It’s our first primary endorsement in four years — after a cycle spent
defending the Squad — and it reflects what Justice Democrats was built
for: challenging the power of millionaires, corporations, and political
insiders by electing working-class leaders who fight for all of us.

Donavan McKinney is exactly that kind of leader. A Black, working-class
organizer from the Detroit area, Donavan knows what it’s like to struggle
and still choose to fight — for his family, his neighbors, and his
community.

This isn’t just about MI-13, but it’s about the future of the Democratic
Party. Will it be bought and paid for by corporate donors and self-funded
millionaires, or rebuilt by people like Donavan who know what our
communities are up against and have the courage to lead?

name: Hillsdale College via Your America News
subject: Your Supreme Court survey
body:
Your participation in Hillsdale College’s National Survey on the United States Supreme Court is requested.

This sponsored message from Your America News is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | |
---
| | [](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zgi1n0gbigr7fbofp5is97snd4e4ii0v6skcn29g_rp22sh2s8i6eob3c1g6eoj4cph2bs)
---
| | | Dear Friend, Your participation in Hillsdale College's **National Survey on the United States Supreme Court** is requested.

Your response will only take a few minutes, but the subject is crucial to the future of liberty and the separation of powers in America.

The American Founders thought that the proper role of the Supreme Court is to apply the Constitution.

But progressives see the Court differently. They want activist judges to legislate from the bench.
## Do you agree that the role of the Supreme Court is to apply the Constitution as it is written and NOT to make laws or advance a particular policy agenda?
[YES](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zajb8ssgref4vlv2nl3mlr6uufmoljog5h3293r8_rp22sh2s8i6eob3c1g6eoj4cph2bs) [NO](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z1mcvep3be20oeahr5f6le6d8uq3l2f0i0d13t7g_rp22sh2s8i6eob3c1g6eoj4cph2bs) Even worse, progressives dismayed by recent Supreme Court decisions want to "pack" the bench with additional justices to advance a preferred policy agenda.

As Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) put it in a _Boston Globe_ op-ed: "To restore balance and integrity to a broken institution, Congress must expand the Supreme Court by four or more seats."

That is why I'm reaching out to you today...

_What is your opinion about the Supreme Court 's role in our constitutional republic? _

Please share your thoughts with me using the College's **National Survey on the United States Supreme Court** right away.

Your response will help Hillsdale form effective strategies to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty--including the proper role of an independent judiciary that applies the Constitution instead of legislating from the bench.

You can easily complete your **National Survey on the United States Supreme Court** using this secure link: **[https://info.hillsdale.edu/supreme-court-survey](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z4jg0vvbv99ovjbill3eroq87fec3buk3b9234c8_rp22sh2s8i6eob3c1g6eoj4cph2bs)** Thank you for your time and attention--and for your support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn
President, Hillsdale College
Pursuing Truth - Defending Liberty since 1844

This sponsored message from 1600 Daily is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zmc8fn4473j1fr4lcj10dir86sl0mqlq9cq842j0_rp22sh2s8i6eob3c1g6eoj4c3h2bs)

I am excited to announce that Hillsdale's online teaching series, ["Supply-Side Economics and American Prosperity with Arthur Laffer,"](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zg0758op3hucrojers9a0ci4dtn8vcop0q2fq50o_rp22sh2s8i6eob3c1g6eoj4c3h2bs) is now available to own as a DVD box set.

In this series, you will discover how taxation, regulation, money, government spending, and trade influence our decisions and impact our lives. Joined by Steve Forbes, Stephen Moore, Larry Kudlow, Amity Shlaes, Brian Domitrovic, and Larry P. Arnn, Dr. Laffer explains how supply-side economics holds the key to unleashing American prosperity once again.

But we need the support of citizens like you to promote this series to millions of Americans along with our other nationwide outreach.

Will you partner with us to promote this free online teaching series from Hillsdale College and expand other educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty? Your tax-deductible donation will help us to enroll thousands of Americans in this series.

And for a donation of $100 or more, we will send you this beautiful DVD box set of "Supply-Side Economics and American Prosperity with Arthur Laffer."

**To help support this course and get your copy of "Supply-Side Economics and American Prosperity with Arthur Laffer" on DVD, click the link below:**

[https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/supply-side-economics-support-dvd](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z6nd0rn09ovftuqsn3ltu54mtka0b48qg4120848_rp22sh2s8i6eob3c1g6eoj4c3h2bs)

I hope you enjoy this teaching series. Thank you for your support.

Warm Regards,

Jeremiah Regan, Ph.D.

name: No Dem Left Behind
subject: Economy Watch: April 30th, 2025
body:
The Port of Los Angeles has recorded a 10% drop compared to last year's numbers.
| | | | | |
---
**_Economy Watch_**
---
Hello, friend! **Welcome back to _Economy Watch_ ,** our weekly newsletter breaking down what’s really happening in the economy. I’m Zoltan Nemeth, and every Wednesday, alongside my colleagues Olya Makarova and Hassan Martini, we cut through the noise to bring you the latest economic developments and what they mean for working Americans. **Here's what's going on right now.**
---
| | | | **Drop in Shipping and Supply Chain Chaos**
---
|
---
For months, tariff talks have felt speculative, **but now, the consequences are undeniable.** China has already sent two empty tankers back to their ports, signaling the damage to their economy. Meanwhile, the Port of Los Angeles is reporting a **10% drop in shipping traffic** compared to this time last year, and officials are warning that a 35% decline in cargo is expected by next week as shipments from China cease entirely. Gene Seroka, Executive Director of the Port of Los Angeles, recently warned that Trump's 90-day pause on "reciprocal" tariffs made no real difference for businesses. Retailers typically place orders months in advance, **and now, orders have dried up.** Exporters in agriculture, heavy-duty manufacturing, and tech services are getting "hit hard" by retaliatory tariffs. In fact, China just bought more soybeans from Brazil than ever before, completely bypassing U.S. farmers. Retailers are sitting on just six to eight weeks of inventory, but without urgent changes, those supplies will quickly run out. Seroka put it bluntly: U.S. consumers and manufacturers will soon face "difficult decisions," **with empty shelves looming.** Even if Trump reversed every tariff today, the damage is already done. Prices are rising, uncertainty is growing, and the effects will linger. How long and how deep this pain will go remains unclear. Major logistics firm Flexport reports that shipping cancellations from China have already hit 50%. Apollo Global Management forecasts that by late May, domestic freight demand could "come to a halt," leading to empty shelves, mass layoffs in trucking and retail sectors, and a full-blown recession this summer. Meanwhile, Trump’s first 100 days have been disastrous for the stock market, **the worst start for a president since Richard Nixon’s second term.** The S&P 500 is down 7.9% since Inauguration Day, wiping out all post-election gains. Container liners, trucking companies, and retailers like Amazon and Target are suffering heavy losses, while America’s economic standing weakens and other nations turn to China for trade partnerships. Those with more wealth can absorb these shocks. But everyday Americans, **who spend most of their paycheck on goods and services,** are already cutting back. Working families are being hit first and hardest by Trump’s reckless policies. **We can’t afford to sit back and watch this happen. It’s time to hold Trump accountable and demand real leadership that puts American workers and families first.**
---
|
---
In solidarity, Zoltan Nemeth

Friend,
The Chinese Communist Party has played us like a fiddle for DECADES.
**And the D.C. Swamp let them.**
They’ve _stolen our technology_ , _gutted our factories_ , and _sold us back cheap goods made with slave labor_. While American workers got squeezed, the CCP made a killing as our politicians looked the other way.
**That ends NOW.**

President Trump did what every career politician in Washington has been too afraid to do -**he drew a hard line in the sand with bold new tariffs to rein in China’s and the CCP’s stranglehold on America.**
**_[Now it’s your move](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/apaj/?__vbtrk=Mjg3ODA4OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjg3ODA4OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_.**
[SIGN NOW: HOLD THE LINE AGAINST CHINA](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/apaj/?__vbtrk=Mjg3ODA4OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjg3ODA4OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
| | This is what putting America First ACTUALLY looks like. Not words. Not handshakes. Real action that is making a difference.
This is making the FAKE news media lose its mind. The globalists who have been filling their pockets are in a meltdown and the CCP is scrambling to divide us because they know if America stands strong then their entire strategy will collapse.
**That’s why I’ve been fighting them from inside Congress with my LAND Act - a bill to block China from buying up American farmland and planting themselves near our military bases.**
They're not buying land. They're buying position. Intel. Leverage.
This is slow-motion warfare, and we’re done playing defense.
**President Trump and I see exactly what China’s doing and we’re not letting them turn America into their doormat.**
Friend, this is chance to hit back.
They’ve used Wall Street, the fake news media, and weak career politicians to erode us from the inside out.
Now that Trump’s stepping in, the knives are out and they’re coming after every voice that refuses to bend the knee, including ME.
**_[So please add your name to this official letter of support today to stand with me, and with President Trump, to support our efforts to Hold The Line against China](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/apaj/?__vbtrk=Mjg3ODA4OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjg3ODA4OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_****.**

## Trump Marks 100 Days With Michigan Rally
President Trump marked [100 days into his second term](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGunjAQBODTQGe02GCgcJGG7qVNiQxew0YGI3v5CbePeFd49Uij-ebP1_RlKdCx_rY7GvZxOvDOAZkxTZyu_cw1gLNPtvtMH0yc7eEmCbIV0AgFk7MUnqkpnfGIElWJpu4aDdC1gyw3o2VvdT_XvZQzDjD00ra68b3Syg26nUsybxs0CmoALYdq6HznQdWtqjXM2BYNoCOOqfob6eANfXjiB1O1xL0MZmM-c6F-FXIs5Hjfd-Xjv1fx5oUczxiIacmFHL9BguPFWewxs8jXsmDO_grCU8osagDxasWZMJPDg8kGsVHmmB7hrkTHKnZaNlrtIZIN4SmTcedNIVDWXdHAulsK39v4R4d-jPwfAAD___L9jFY) Tuesday with a rally in Michigan, highlighting recent executive actions and restating key policy goals. Hours before the rally, Trump signed [executive orders scaling back a scheduled 25% tariff](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHO4yAQBOCnwZ2jBQw4BcU17nLtlRY2S7wnbCJYJ5e3PyWv8Lcz0ifN_LnNt0CZjvvvsKPnVOYDXy0jM9aZ67k_mgSI4d3CvtATK7dwxFmBMj0MvYY5BsrveeiiT4gKdYdeusECOHNV3eaNlHZ0btE2DaDdmOyarNSQotFyHGNH_qPBoEECWHW9XF1yCbQ0WlpY0IgBMBKXevlb6OANU36XJ9bLWvYu-4350YT-JdQk1MQbbpTzpxNqWs5GB7Ym1BTLjo1p7Tn8w09glNNgdf9d2YeTS8-hUkqtrxjPlakcQk1d9fHxopypWScGuO-BvnzHP_rr6dX_AAAA__8yPX18) on imported cars and parts, allowing automakers to apply for phased-in price offsets—15% in the first year and 10% in the second—before full rates take effect. Speaking for over 90 minutes, Trump hailed what he called the “most successful 100 days” in U.S. history, citing mass deportations, revived tariffs, and a renewed push to end birthright citizenship. Supporters gathered inside the venue while demonstrators protested outside.
## Canada's Liberal Party Wins the Election
Canada's Liberal Party, led by Prime Minister Mark Carney, has [won a fourth consecutive term](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ8GOqLxH4bCxW3S5bZbosEzTrwyGBkvEW-_Iq-w5dGRjs73fT2mB8YU1-d_XNjVkKeV33viWrlMtfws2y4ACM8dlzkeXOqOK00SpOlAdwomwpjOSbfkArNk1bITVvcA1oyyfbmZzTAEG3AUtmczGM8-sDbEoEYvsY3uWgOtQAD0cryNNtgAShglepjZNBqYYs3l9p3jWl8c0pkPLjeflza5V63b3qh_jbw38o7bBXBVVyg1-sSNvHtckbDjxL7GvHYey8pn9yHsthxT5KNwZ0lLkjSqeRxIW-Elhll56kGSEJba4mh7x5Ti3ttGw3PBmD4_6p_kHU7-BgAA___YkIJB), securing 169 seats in the House of Commons--just shy of a majority. The Conservative Party, under Pierre Poilievre, finished with 144 seats, while the Bloc Quebecois and New Democratic Party (NDP) captured 23 and seven seats, respectively. [See charts here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OqzAUBOCnMV3Q8R8OhYvb0OW2WyKbc5w4MjiyvSDefsW-wnYjjfRJM1-P-eFiitvzv1vJtpDnjY6aqDUqcyvf66dyAHRndauPO5VW3YazAKFvoG4SZnQxnbPq0AYiQbIjy40aAIweRfeygAR-NAHl_a5JoSYvDSIXMAQ_oO6ivTRQEjjAIMZ-NMEEkFxLPoAnzRQQxpZL_85xay8K6cw7lX7Ja5fsq7VPZfIfExMT03EcvffL1TExXWOYmFxpcUl0xWVTb5Tj837y3BWLnyOmFOtgmILn6mL6Vdufrtit-AkAAP__untw8Q). Both Poilievre and NDP leader Jagmeet Singh lost their own ridings, with Singh subsequently announcing his resignation. Carney, positioning himself as a defender of Canadian sovereignty, [declared in his victory speech](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L9OwzAQgPGncbZW5_OfqwcPCCkDUlkZI4ecW4OTVLabkrdH5RVYv-E3fB_n4RxSTsvlPczsW1yHhR81c2tchlbu861KgCnsNcxj2ri0GpZpQEBzAH1QMEwh5X3Q3eQjM7Lq2EvSFoCMw-7qkaKBwM5YDZrUydowRqesgRON0eku-acGWoEEsOiOjiJFUNIoaWFkIzTwlNpajl9rWtqVY97Xjcvxc5277K-t3apQLwJ7gf3Pswrsz6F8v72GsvAusK8ttHsV2MuT04bIKI2GkJwE6oqfbo-Uc6qWhIbLHFL-s9u_hmwefwMAAP__WO1vXA) that Canada would never "be part of the United States in any way, shape or form."
## $60 Million Navy Jet Lost During Houthi Attack
A $60 million U.S. Navy F/A-18E Super Hornet [jet was lost at sea on Monday](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE8DmVFjDIjAwSZks-mGqLHbg0fmR-0eELdf8a7woiqppFJ99e81vTCmuL3_4kpWwj5tdOVEIsST8Hc9cg3g8c64zvEkloybnzToVoFRDUweY7onU3obiDQ1Jdm6Nx1A3w66XGznCEJv5t60LnhnvEEMAZwJMCAaX0b7tIFpoAbo9FANfegDNHXb1B3M1BYGyEfZufrscZOFQrr3k7hy-1omu4gcuWj-FHos9HhdV-Xm_FA8eaHHxz6C562-OasFmW_1sOGmMLJjDKIcMkdilfZMWeXvQayWnTcSFeJ7EWL1IVFMXmXCQo8lW39cMaWYu74w8F4xpp9J8qsfT6v_BwAA__-gtInP) after falling overboard from the USS Harry S. Truman during an evasive maneuver to avoid incoming fire from Yemen-based Houthi rebels. The aircraft, under tow inside the hangar bay, and its tow tractor slipped into the Red Sea as the carrier turned sharply amid the ongoing threat. All crew members escaped safely, though one sailor suffered a minor injury. [Watch a video report here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LtuxCAQheGnwd1aw4BNXFDkou02VaSUCC_jNQm-CGbt-O2jzSukPUf6iv_z4i4-pjjf3v1ElofFzbSXRMyUHef7tBYJEPxR_NTHjTIXPweHgM0J9EmBCz6mw-kq2IEISVVkpdEtgGk6rEYrfR806hA6RUiSND51fefBoAQDJKtoHxpoBRKgxa7uzGAGULJRsoWeGqGBQuQl119LnHmkIR3LRrm-LlOV7Mi8FqGeBZ4Fnvd9r4_lzveeHv9j8XwdhTpvQr3pl4_X4n7W4_ZdZRvWPaYUS2uEhtvkY_oj-V8dNou_AQAA__8XJW_F). The jet is part of an extended deployment supporting [Operation Rough Rider](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQRp_G7lgN4J-4oEjjbtOmtLAZzEQYLBh7tW8f7b2PcOtP-nTO-ftcnpYipf2PPdCwz0vCV43IjGXhch1nlQDOvqs9VrqxcLXJLQpUL6ATGhZnKb6XrnXGIyrULRo5dgPA2E-qDUaBnHrtdN9L8JuT4-T06jc_Kae0VmtL5vMGnQYJMKjpMY1-9KBlr-UAK_ZNB-iIc3n8y5Q4oI_vfGN5bPloownMZ23070bNjZr3zZ5sKX3GRs35xGKZchIlX3sQhRwW8S0msveYKt0oAnEVvwBEyBcHEmzLjlyFraIGOk9Ku9gKVapiy4kpXVgbNbfFuPNFMVIdxqaD_bAUv7D4Ry1vo_4HAAD__2etikM), the largest U.S. air campaign since the ISIS fight, targeting Houthi missile and drone operators. The Houthis, backed by Iran, have brought down more than a dozen U.S. drones in recent months and continue to threaten commercial and military vessels in the region.

# [In 1908, there was a car race from New York to Paris.](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svj0rx&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
### [Science & Industry](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svj0rx&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svj0rx&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
| I n the early 20th century, when automobiles were in their infancy, the idea of driving long distances was still ambitious. But that was precisely the challenge of the 1908 [New York to Paris race](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svj0rx&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), a bold, 22,000-mile competition that spanned three continents during the dead of winter. On the morning of February 12, six teams representing four countries — France, Germany, Italy, and the United States — gathered in front of 250,000 spectators in Times Square in New York City. The cars and their teams, made up of drivers, mechanics, and journalists, departed at 11:15 a.m. The American Thomas Flyer car quickly pulled into the lead. Behind it came Italy’s Zust, Germany’s Protos, and three entries from France — a Motobloc, a De Dion, and a Sizaire-Naudin (the latter broke down and dropped out of the race after just 96 miles).
---
The ambitious plan was for the teams to reach San Francisco within 22 days; from there, a ship would take them to Alaska, where they would drive across a presumably frozen Bering Strait into Siberia, continue across Russia and Europe, and finally reach Paris. But the race didn’t exactly take place as planned. The cars took twice that time to reach the West Coast, and the spring thaw made the Alaskan route too difficult. Competitors were instead rerouted to Seattle, shipped across the Pacific to Japan, and then shipped again across the Sea of Japan to Vladivostok, Russia.
Along the way, drivers endured blizzards, sandstorms, and nearly impassable roads — if there were roads at all. Mechanical problems, personnel changes, and visa delays also caused setbacks. In the end, just three of the original six cars completed the journey. On July 30, the Thomas Flyer finally reached Paris. A police officer initially refused to let the car proceed with its broken headlight, but a passerby offered up a bicycle light. Though the Protos had technically arrived three days earlier, organizers issued a penalty for shortcuts taken along the way. So at 6 p.m., after a 169-day journey, the American car officially won the great race.

## Thomas Edison and Henry Ford developed an electric car together.
Henry Ford and Thomas Edison's friendship has been well documented, and along with their shared vacation homes and [camping trips](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svj0rx&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), the two collaborated on new technology together. In January 1914, Ford confirmed to _The_ _New York Times_ that he was working with Edison on a low-cost, long-range [electric vehicle](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svj0rx&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com). Edison worked to design a durable battery that was also lightweight, and Ford planned to manufacture the cars in a new plant to be run by his son, Edsel Ford. At least two known prototypes were built: a tiller-steered design with batteries under the seat, and a second design that incorporated elements from the Model T along with a different motor position and an extra bank of batteries. Despite high expectations, the project never went to market. Edison’s nickel-iron batteries were still too big and inefficient, and refinements to it were quickly outpaced by improvements in fuel engines and infrastructure. By the 1920s, Ford and Edison had quietly abandoned the idea.

clean_body: In the early 20th century, when automobiles were in their infancy, the idea of driving long distances was still ambitious. | I n the early 20th century, when automobiles were in their infancy, the idea of driving long distances was still ambitious. But that was precisely the challenge of the 1908 , a bold, 22,000-mile competition that spanned three continents during the dead of winter. On the morning of February 12, six teams representing four countries — France, Germany, Italy, and the United States — gathered in front of 250,000 spectators in Times Square in New York City. The cars and their teams, made up of drivers, mechanics, and journalists, departed at 11:15 a.m. The American Thomas Flyer car quickly pulled into the lead. Behind it came Italy’s Zust, Germany’s Protos, and three entries from France — a Motobloc, a De Dion, and a Sizaire-Naudin (the latter broke down and dropped out of the race after just 96 miles). The ambitious plan was for the teams to reach San Francisco within 22 days; from there, a ship would take them to Alaska, where they would drive across a presumably frozen Bering Strait into Siberia, continue across Russia and Europe, and finally reach Paris. But the race didn’t exactly take place as planned. The cars took twice that time to reach the West Coast, and the spring thaw made the Alaskan route too difficult. Competitors were instead rerouted to Seattle, shipped across the Pacific to Japan, and then shipped again across the Sea of Japan to Vladivostok, Russia. Along the way, drivers endured blizzards, sandstorms, and nearly impassable roads — if there were roads at all. Mechanical problems, personnel changes, and visa delays also caused setbacks. In the end, just three of the original six cars completed the journey. On July 30, the Thomas Flyer finally reached Paris. A police officer initially refused to let the car proceed with its broken headlight, but a passerby offered up a bicycle light. Though the Protos had technically arrived three days earlier, organizers issued a penalty for shortcuts taken along the way. So at 6 p.m., after a 169-day journey, the American car officially won the great race. | By clicking a link in this email, you're agreeing to our and . Henry Ford and Thomas Edison's friendship has been well documented, and along with their shared vacation homes and , the two collaborated on new technology together. In January 1914, Ford confirmed to The New York Times that he was working with Edison on a low-cost, long-range . Edison worked to design a durable battery that was also lightweight, and Ford planned to manufacture the cars in a new plant to be run by his son, Edsel Ford. At least two known prototypes were built: a tiller-steered design with batteries under the seat, and a second design that incorporated elements from the Model T along with a different motor position and an extra bank of batteries. Despite high expectations, the project never went to market. Edison’s nickel-iron batteries were still too big and inefficient, and refinements to it were quickly outpaced by improvements in fuel engines and infrastructure. By the 1920s, Ford and Edison had quietly abandoned the idea. ## Mexico Agrees to Water Deal
Mexico has agreed to a deal aimed at [alleviating a severe water shortage](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGuqzAQRVcDndFgbAiFi9_Q5bevRMYzBCsGR_YQyO6fyBZefaWje87PfbxbH_z2-G9XMnzOcdzoyIGYKY2HZUpINkRHIbKLK03WPe02SpBagBINjGh9-IyqRDMB9nVJpu5UCzXculu5GCKNSkPfaI2AXac0qoZUO2vbT65TpTcXDFQDdQ11raupoQn1DeQ8t30HWCgg9BxTxQsxnTbP4RPflCoX1zKYhfmVi-ZfIYdCDsdxVHM8L4trL-TwisGzd7mQw-UiMqfdPcWexUqnd1HQlvdE4osWs00rpSwexGLd3SI2IiQU3xZlMvg6fAg-t12h4LFaH743-G_x3kb-BgAA__8KnoaK) in South Texas caused in part by Mexico’s failure to abide by a 1944 treaty that requires it to send 1.75 million acre-feet of water to the U.S. every five years. Mexico will send [up to 420,000 acre-feet to South Texas](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSoyAURp8GO5wLatCCYhu7bLulc4VLwiyIAxjj2_-TvMLff_OdOefffbmjD357_MVIur5dWjY6S6BaKS8nVsqWMCRDIVWTIq1o_uO2SJADh553sFj04Vr6xuoV7CQa0kL1NxAwqrF5aokwopukmlA4103WgcKhVys50SkzNl5_zqDvQAgQYmjXjlY7jCCdu00KLOuBrK8pt_VJld5YXLjSi3JrUmyCfta6F9b9YXJmcj7Ps31hCHQZ2mrG8FkxOZsU47H5ejE5H7zwSG9vEv_YcdrKkanwry8vx76Hi7uU-ZfG8ZG9OUI9MjE5N1nb_fQh-HJTrIdHRP-FNPV3AV9a_gQAAP__qIeIcA) by October, the end of the current five-year period. So far, Mexico has delivered less than 600,000 acre-feet during this cycle. To address [the projected shortfall](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGysyAUBOCn0Q7nAIqxoPibdPnbWzpHOEYmIA6QkLz9HfMKt9_Z2W9_bvMNnXf7_T8G0uW9xnmnmj2VQmmuWChZQh8N-VhMDLSgeeA-CxADg55JmC06_5n71uoF7MRb0nzsFXC4jJd204uSiItBQC4EKewnXBUME9jJoJSidfosg14C58D50C2SFjtcQKyrmkawTQ9kXYmpKxsVemNe_Se-KHUmhtbrrZQjN_JfI66NuNZau5NQiR5noBHXkp7hYGiD21nAB2X2hbFTxgK9nYnsSJSdpb0w4_FpHbK8kdsXfAYmQA2SqzZpe1TnvctqbHq4B3T-u6H87bmXFr8BAAD__4wFhLc), Mexico will make monthly transfers from two Rio Grande reservoirs and provide the U.S. with half of the flow—rather than a third—from six of its tributaries. The agreement provides a measure of relief for South Texas farmers and ranchers who have [struggled amid an ongoing drought](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uhDAQBOCnMZ3R-oe_wkUaukubEi14fVgx-ASb893bR-QVUo80o2--btMNY4r7_RM3cvwKedqpnImY6ZgKMh2eMOWFUuYlbzTj8o37pEE3Eqw0MHmM6T3ZyrsZ_KAqcqqzLSjou75aXRuU6aEfYJ7bLlATGtOSQa1wAOobqqK7ysAaUAqUaurZ0OybHnQI7dCBFxbIR85HzSsxvfAM6Z2fdNRL3qrkVubHKcyH0KPQYymlfuOa85UKPV4coccfudErLlni_SCSF0qetPtTagBjjdJdvfKWqsP5R4kpxbPthIX7hjH9DfH_7nk6_RsAAP__mdJ4rw) that has threatened the region’s citrus industry and shut down its last sugar mill last year.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 4/30/2025
body:
Clock runs out on social media bill: lawmakers shield themselves and Polis from historic override
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi folks,
Listen to today's **Mountain Minute Podcast** [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)! Here is a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Colorado Legislative Session Updates...** Colorado lawmakers quietly killed a bipartisan override of Gov. Polis’s veto on a [social media bill](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) by voting to delay action until after session, avoiding a formal vote. Meanwhile, with an important vote TODAY, Southern Baptists are urging [opposition to HB25-1312](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), citing threats to parental rights and religious liberty. Colorado GOP leaders also asked U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi to investigate the [state’s latest gun laws](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), calling them unconstitutional.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A town hall in Greeley drew over 100 participants, but critics say it felt more like a [political playbook](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) than a grassroots forum. The event, titled “Where is Gabe?”, criticized Rep. Gabe Evans for not attending—even though Evans has been active on public safety and education, and was recently endorsed by President Trump. Meanwhile, the Trump administration [pulled $32 million in FEMA grants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) from Denver’s immigrant shelters, citing the city’s sanctuary status and failure to cooperate with ICE.
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** President Trump signed an executive order [targeting sanctuary cities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), threatening to cut federal funds from those that defy immigration laws and blocking benefits for illegal immigrants. Meanwhile, a [new progressive bloc](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—the “Urbanist Party” led by Sanders, AOC, and David Hogg—is gaining steam, sparking talk of a 2028 challenge to Kamala Harris.
🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** Today's commentary section tackles two urgent truths: George Tristan compares [President Trump’s first 100 days](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to a national home renovation—touting immigration victories, economic momentum, and plans to “flush out” woke influence in public education. Meanwhile, Greg Walcher calls out the federal red tape [strangling America’s inner cities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), arguing that bureaucratic overreach—not infrastructure—keeps redevelopment projects from ever breaking ground.

This is the Mountain Minute for Wednesday, April 30, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Clock runs out on social media bill: lawmakers shield themselves and Polis from historic override](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Without casting a single “no” vote, Colorado lawmakers on April 28 killed a bipartisan attempt to override Governor Jared Polis’ veto of a social media regulation bill. Just days earlier, the Senate had voted 29–6 to override the veto of Senate Bill 25-086, marking the state’s first successful chamber override of a policy bill in more than a decade.
But when the bill reached the House, members voted 51–13 to lay over the override until after the legislative session ended. As reported by The Colorado Sun, the maneuver guaranteed the bill’s death without a formal vote, allowing lawmakers to avoid public reversals and preserving Polis from a rare legislative rebuke.
The decision to delay was no accident. Under Colorado legislative rules, any business scheduled after the session’s final day—May 7—is automatically void.

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Was it the people’s town hall — or a political playbook in action?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* A progressive-organized event in Greeley titled “Where is Gabe?” gave nearly 50 residents three minutes each to share concerns about representation, unity, and Rep. Gabe Evans’ absence, emphasizing grassroots voices over a central speaker.
* Despite its civic tone, the town hall was part of a broader Democrat strategy to flip Colorado’s 8th District, using symbolic props, media blitzes, and national figures like AOC. Evans' team called the criticism staged and pointed to his public service record.
* While critics saw campaign tactics at play, the event underscored a broader statewide demand for face-to-face engagement and civic accountability—echoing growing calls across Colorado for more responsive leadership.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Southern Baptist group urges Colorado pastors, members to oppose transgender rights bill](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Center for Baptist Leadership is urging over 300 Colorado churches to oppose the bill, citing threats to parental rights, religious liberty, and free speech due to penalties for “misgendering” and “deadnaming.”
* The bill would require courts to consider gender identity disputes in custody decisions and could penalize parents for not affirming a child’s gender identity—raising alarms among faith-based groups.
* The group Fight 1312 is organizing a rally before the Senate Judiciary hearing, calling the bill an attack on “God-given liberties” and encouraging pastors and congregants to speak out.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[FEMA cuts $32 million from Denver’s immigrant shelter grants under Trump directive](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Trump administration ended $32 million in FEMA grants to Denver, stating the city’s support for illegal immigrants through shelter, transport, and services conflicts with federal enforcement priorities.
* The city has spent over $80 million supporting 43,000 migrants since 2023. Officials say Denver’s reputation as a “welcoming” city—and its public opposition to mass deportations—contributed to the funding cut.
* Denver may be required to repay funds spent after March 11. The canceled aid was intended for food, shelter, medical care, and hygiene support for undocumented migrants awaiting removal proceedings.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[Tristan: Trump’s first 100 days prove America’s home improvement is not about reality show illusions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY GEORGE TRISTAN****| COMMENTARY | APRIL 29** _There are many home improvement reality shows on television today. Every episode, following completion of the project, culminates in the highly anticipated “reveal.”_
**[Walcher: We built it, and they still won’t come](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY GREG WALCHER | COMMENTARY | APRIL 29** _Building a new subdivision is complicated. Almost every city and county in America have master plans dictating “conforming uses” of land. Most specify lot and home sizes, rules for vehicle access, water supply, sewage disposal, flood control, affordable housing, and park space._
**[HB25-1312 Scheduled for Senate Judiciary Hearing Wednesday: How to Participate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY RMV STAFF | STATE | APRIL 28** _It was more than just another Tuesday morning at Valor Christian High School in Highlands Ranch, Colorado—it was a full-on Turning Point. Nearly 50 students, faculty, and guests gathered for the official launch of Valor’s new Turning Point USA chapter, and let’s just say, the energy was more electric than a Bronco game on a Sunday afternoon._

But when the bill reached the House, members voted 51–13 to lay over the override until after the legislative session ended. As reported by The Colorado Sun, the maneuver guaranteed the bill’s death without a formal vote, allowing lawmakers to avoid public reversals and preserving Polis from a rare legislative rebuke. The decision to delay was no accident. Under Colorado legislative rules, any business scheduled after the session’s final day—May 7—is automatically void. | The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support! | A progressive-organized event in Greeley titled “Where is Gabe?” gave nearly 50 residents three minutes each to share concerns about representation, unity, and Rep. Gabe Evans’ absence, emphasizing grassroots voices over a central speaker. Despite its civic tone, the town hall was part of a broader Democrat strategy to flip Colorado’s 8th District, using symbolic props, media blitzes, and national figures like AOC. Evans' team called the criticism staged and pointed to his public service record. While critics saw campaign tactics at play, the event underscored a broader statewide demand for face-to-face engagement and civic accountability—echoing growing calls across Colorado for more responsive leadership. | The Center for Baptist Leadership is urging over 300 Colorado churches to oppose the bill, citing threats to parental rights, religious liberty, and free speech due to penalties for “misgendering” and “deadnaming.” The bill would require courts to consider gender identity disputes in custody decisions and could penalize parents for not affirming a child’s gender identity—raising alarms among faith-based groups. The group Fight 1312 is organizing a rally before the Senate Judiciary hearing, calling the bill an attack on “God-given liberties” and encouraging pastors and congregants to speak out. | The Trump administration ended $32 million in FEMA grants to Denver, stating the city’s support for illegal immigrants through shelter, transport, and services conflicts with federal enforcement priorities. The city has spent over $80 million supporting 43,000 migrants since 2023. Officials say Denver’s reputation as a “welcoming” city—and its public opposition to mass deportations—contributed to the funding cut. Denver may be required to repay funds spent after March 11. The canceled aid was intended for food, shelter, medical care, and hygiene support for undocumented migrants awaiting removal proceedings. | ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ BY GEORGE TRISTAN**| COMMENTARY | APRIL 29 There are many home improvement reality shows on television today. Every episode, following completion of the project, culminates in the highly anticipated “reveal.” BY GREG WALCHER | COMMENTARY | APRIL 29 Building a new subdivision is complicated. Almost every city and county in America have master plans dictating “conforming uses” of land. Most specify lot and home sizes, rules for vehicle access, water supply, sewage disposal, flood control, affordable housing, and park space. BY RMV STAFF | STATE | APRIL 28 It was more than just another Tuesday morning at Valor Christian High School in Highlands Ranch, Colorado—it was a full-on Turning Point. subject: 1985 A Macintosh Moment: Trusting My Instincts Over Common Sense
body:
A 40th Anniversary of my first Macintosh

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us16.campaign-archive.com/?e=8763c56857&u=ebcefd906ec01db66e79c886c&id=53ba1684bc)

| | | | |

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | “We are here to make a dent in the universe”Steve Jobs
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
|
---
|
---
| **Opinion | A personal story worth sharing**
**1985 A Macintosh Moment: Trusting My Instincts Over Common Sense**
_By Dominic Rapini, CEO, Queralt, Inc_
In 1985, I was a biology teacher at a private school in Connecticut, making just enough to keep my ‘69 Chevy Nova alive and maybe splurge on a decent bowl of pasta every now and then. One Saturday, I tagged along with my friend Dan, a fellow teacher, to a computer store—back when computer stores felt like a cross between a sci-fi gift shop and a RadioShack with a caffeine problem.
Dan was there to buy a computer. I was just along for the ride.
He bailed. I didn’t.
I walked out with a brand-new Macintosh, an external floppy drive, an ImageWriter printer, and a $4,500 credit card bill I had no business racking up. I probably should’ve spent that money on a better car—or, you know, student loans —but something about that Mac pulled me in. I brought it home, sat down at 6 p.m., and didn’t get up until the sun rose the next morning.
I didn’t fully realize it at the time, but that moment ‘reprogrammed’ my life.
Almost immediately, I’ve begun to put that Macintosh to work. I was doing student comments on three-part carbon forms. I was running the forms through the dot matrix printer for my students, automating every crazy, tedious task. I was doing diagrams of cell structures and biology processes and incorporating them in handouts and eventually putting on transparencies up on an overhead projector. I was using the Macintosh to design pages for my football playbook and on, and on, and on. That crazy investment was already reshaping my life and the way I worked, and opening up incredible opportunities and possibilities. My imagination was on fire with all the ideas and the ways to apply this technology and all the great software into everyday solutions.
Months later, I was helping design one of the first computer labs in U.S. education. A year after that, I left teaching and jumped into computer retail. Before long, I became an expert in desktop publishing and corporate networking. Cybersecurity back then? It meant locking your floppy disks in a file cabinet. (No joke. That was “zero trust.”)
Then, in 1997, I made another decision that raised a few eyebrows. I joined Apple.
Now, keep in mind—this was not today’s Apple. This was “$4 billion in revenue and a tanking stock price” Apple. The general industry sentiment was: Apple is toast. Michael Dell famously said the best thing Apple could do was shut down and return the money to shareholders.
But a month earlier, Steve Jobs had returned to the company. And while Wall Street saw a company on life support, my instincts told me something else: this was the beginning of a comeback story. I trusted that feeling—and it paid off.
Four decades later, I’m still in tech. And I’m still glad I listened to my gut. Today for really the first time in 40 years I’m starting this see once again the incredible opportunities and possibilities around technology that I first experience in April 1985 but today it’s artificial intelligence and all the new tools that I’ve embraced in the last two years that are changing the way I do my work quite frankly these are tools that are so powerful that they empowered me to jump out of retirement and take over a company as a CEO, where AI becomes a multiplier for my talents and allow me to do the work of 10 people at times leveraging my creativity in my ideas and translating my thoughts into actions
In my lifetime, God has blessed me to witness one **revolution** , more than most people ever get. I’m seeing a whole second **revolution** that if you excuse, the hyperbole is changing my life and the life of all humanity, man is that awesome or what, it all started with this really bad idea spending more money than I had on a technology that I didn’t understand yet I technology that changed the trajectory of my entire life
Recently, that instinct pulled me out of retirement and into a whole new challenge: cybersecurity. It’s the fastest-moving, most unpredictable space I’ve ever worked in—and I’ve seen some wild ones. But I love it. I’m now helping build a product designed to eliminate passwords and save people from the kind of financial damage phishing causes every day.
What’s the lesson here? **Sometimes, the smartest moves start out looking like the crazy ones.** There’s no playbook for spotting the right opportunity at the right time. Sometimes all you’ve got is a hunch and a heart that won’t shut up. Learn to trust that.
Today, I tell young people just starting out: your next job—or the job you’ll have five years from now—might not even exist yet. With AI reshaping everything faster than we can explain it, that’s more true than ever. The key is staying ready. Stay curious. Keep learning. Don’t get too complacent with your current skill set.
And when it comes to advice?**Listen to friends. Listen to mentors. But never let them have the final word.** That’s yours. Take everything you’ve lived and learned, and let that guide you.
Learn to recognize opportunity, learn to recognize when a revolution is upon you.
Ironically, some friends told me I should just enjoy retirement. Maybe take up **fishing** but I resisted. And now here I am—building a **phishing** -resistant software platform instead. Life’s funny like that.
We’re all wired with intuition for a reason. Sometimes, you’ve got to lean in, take the leap, and trust that voice in your head that says, This might actually work.
It just might.

"**The Texas House wants voters to approve billions to save the state 's water supply**," Texas Tribune's **Jayme Lozano Carver** \-- "The Texas House on Tuesday approved a key piece of legislation that brings Texas one step closer to investing $1 billion annually to address the state's water shortage.

[House Joint Resolution 7](https://substack.com/redirect/b2519ff8-d5f5-485b-b624-d9105d4f2b32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), led by state Rep. **Cody Harris** , R-Palestine, was overwhelmingly approved by the lower chamber, 138-6. Tuesday's vote sets the proposal on a path to voters. If the Senate also approves it, voters will be asked in November to approve the spending, which comes from the state's sales tax.

The Senate has a similar proposal, asking voters for dedicated funding. However, it spells out how the money is to be used. Written by state Sen. **Charles Perry** , R-Lubbock, [Senate Joint Resolution 66](https://substack.com/redirect/88593a10-2fd4-45ab-9ae9-327354f99e6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) calls for 80% of the $1 billion to go toward projects that create new water supply, such as desalination or produced water treatment plants. The remaining 20% would be split among several programs that address other needs, including infrastructure upgrades for aging pipes, drinking water and wastewater treatment plants.
