body:
It was a big week at Forward - here's what you missed.

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=1)
---
Wednesday, April 30, 2025 | Peter -- In the last two weeks, we asked about how economic policy affects your personal lives (think cost of living), and your thoughts on the larger economic issues facing the country (think national debt). This week, we continued our _**Controlling What You Can**_ __ series by taking a look one step further. With the tariffs the Trump administration is implementing these past few months, trade has been the main topic of nearly every political talk show, pundit, and news program. So we asked you what you think American trade policy should be. Here's what you had to say: In our most one sided set of opinions yet, Forwardists overwhelmingly said that the current U.S. trade policies are hurting their financial situation, with only 6% of our supporters claiming to be helped by the current stances of the administration. When we dove into the details, 83% of you wanted fully free or mostly free trade, while only 17% of you thought that restrictive repatriation tactics were the way to go. You all sounded off in the comment sections on X and our website and two core themes came to the forefront: **Tariffs Hurt The American Consumer And Crush Main Street**
* The tariff program in place currently is creating undue burden on most of your lives. You noted that prices have gone up and with it, your cost of living.
* You called for the openness of trade once more, claiming that open markets lead to more wealth for all - though many of you noted that this system is ripe for exploitation.

**While These Tariffs Are Being Applied Poorly, A Smart Tariff Policy Can Work**
* Blanket tariffs without thought for why or how have hurt the American consumer - on that you all seem to agree. But many of you point out that there can be good uses for Tariffs. They can be used to protect delicate and crucial American industries, or to play hardball with foreign powers that utilize inhumane working conditions or dishonest market practices to stake out their claim in the world market.

[Utah's Newest Political Party Has A New Chair](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=pcSTFyB5C-uh91nt9g2Xy1Z-jU5N1uVObm6Xl31amBujcwA9HBsl41QClIil2hMzpC_MJBgkWrtNOTxlzQtAqS9qHq2qT2Z0TavvDxpMNtcwbGv608AOR2I-IZlbki260vr9t4DWQEvxuiIM5pFTIwm0g__TVNrQdy4Jo4vSxio&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=2) | _Deseret News_ The Utah Forward Party and the United Utah Party merged this past weekend, but that's not all they did. They also elected Michelle Quist to be the new chair of the burgeoning political party. [Forward Party and Forward Ohio Endorse Kate Curry-DaSouza For Columbus City Council](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=4ZphYPhjQhxKf2D9Q-75WjdO2ZSaSdE1WCPeUjw9g_EUtkHil1za7fCG4CN0taYlBam5bZSfwdJBrgymjOqZb8DuZvXM-j9MObfcfhLrChWyMDLXcUKTTgkyUenSS6kXaURf5k5ODpr4h4o7cFyonOn7lL-1jre5ZZRXWKeA-qY&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=3) | _The New Americans Mag_ The Forward Party and Forward Ohio have announced their endorsement of Kate Curry-DaSouza for Columbus City Council. “As an independent candidate, Curry-Da-Souza stands out as a beacon of progress, ready to lead the city towards a brighter, more inclusive future,” said Forward Ohio.
**April 29 | Run For Office With The Forward Party
** Have you ever thought about running for office, but weren't sure if you were the right fit or how you'd even get started? Well Forward has you covered. Join us to learn how it all works and how you can get started! [**Register →**](https://home.forwardparty.com/run_for_office_with_forward_party?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=4) **May 3 | Second Annual Minnesota Convention
** Join the Minnesota Forward Party for their second annual state convention in Mapelwood! Doors open at 10 am on May 3rd! [**Register →**](https://home.forwardparty.com/minnesota_2nd_annual_convention?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=5) **May 4 | Inaugural Massachusetts Forward Party Convention
** The Massachusetts Forward Party holds its first ever convention. Hear from guest speakers, vote on bylaws and the state executive committee, learn more about the policy and platform, and find out how you can get involved! [**Register →**](https://home.forwardparty.com/2025_massachusetts_forward_party_state_convention?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=6) **May 13 | National Volunteer Call
** Join our director of volunteer engagement, Carrie Anne, on the second Tuesday of May at 7:30 PM ET for all things FWD volunteer! Meet other Forwardists and learn how you can get more involved in your community. **[Register →](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20250513_2?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=7)** **May 20 | Women's Committee Priorities Forum
** Join the Forward Party Women's Committee for their 2nd Priorities Forum. This forum is dedicated to shaping the future focus of the committee by identifying the priorities that matter most to the committee members. **[Register →](https://home.forwardparty.com/2nd_fwdwc_priorities_forum?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=8)**
****[Forward Party CEO Joins Sirius XM's The Julie Mason Show](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=vzeQ1nDWVyd5gqyopJ-rriZ6RhD1Oly1GAh2BilmWUdKq3vUMRHQGJuDPobhpGtiXORTEHVKQ3Z_alRZ2t9-0TF3fqycm6dI4M5f6lb0PhcbWpSKDPyn-TbjAMqM14iYwSnlBR8AFUJ85Iuusxucsg&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_61&n=9)** | SIRIUS XM** **[Utah Forward Party and Sen. body:
Trump name-dropped AOC on stage last night.
#
Donald Trump just did something he hasn’t bothered with in a while (maybe because his poll numbers are in free-fall): he dragged himself to Michigan for an actual, in-person event.
**And he opened his rally with a meltdown about Alexandria and Bernie Sanders — claiming our rallies are tiny compared to his. 🙄**
**[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20250430-1.6pzmaT&refcode=em20250430-8725-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=8725%2E2526796%2EJcqntQ)**
Why is he rattled? Because the **Fighting Oligarchy tour is working.**
For weeks, Alexandria, Bernie, and a coalition of progressives have crisscrossed the country — in red, blue, and purple districts alike — rallying tens of thousands against the oligarchs who are rigging our economy to hand billionaires big tax breaks while slashing the public services that benefit working families.
And everywhere they go, energy surges. Local congressmen are reconsidering their votes to cut Medicaid. New volunteers sign up. **Good things happen.**
Trump knows that. So he’s lashing out. **That means our plan is working — and now we need to double down.**
[ Will you donate $5 right now to keep Alexandria on the road, rallying the American people to fight back against Trump and his friends turning the country into their personal slush fund?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20250430-1.6pzmaT&refcode=em20250430-8725-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=8725%2E2526796%2EJcqntQ)

We’ve got him rattled. Now, every dollar we raise helps us apply more pressure to Trump and the oligarchs.
Let’s keep it going.
In solidarity,
Team AOC

In just 100 days in office, President Trump has taken unprecedented action to restrict access to reproductive health care in the U.S. and around the world. His administration is stacked with extreme opponents of reproductive freedom working day and night to undermine the rule of law we depend on to uphold our fundamental rights. **Individually, these officials have great power; together, they will do long-lasting damage to human rights and to our democracy.**

We launched our [**_Repro Red Flags: Agency Watch_**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106796758/542688170/1207998042?sourceid=1150618&utm_campaign=25emcus-0401aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=100days&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyM2U5ZGQxOC1kMzI1LWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cOCD4Itd5xZtuL_idaMeDyy4A-2pjD5nQcX7kM35Ac0=&emci=b4b246f5-3c25-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&emdi=23e9dd18-d325-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=954237) initiative on day one of the Trump administration to connect the dots between key anti-rights officials and the harmful policies they enact. [**At the 100-day mark, we're highlighting President Trump's top five Repro Red Flags**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106796759/542688184/-1147171705?sourceid=1150618&utm_campaign=25emcus-0401aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=100days&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyM2U5ZGQxOC1kMzI1LWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cOCD4Itd5xZtuL_idaMeDyy4A-2pjD5nQcX7kM35Ac0=&emci=b4b246f5-3c25-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&emdi=23e9dd18-d325-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=954237), sounding the alarm about the administration's sweeping attacks on reproductive rights. | [**READ NOW** ](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106796760/542688191/-1147171705?sourceid=1150618&utm_campaign=25emcus-0401aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=100days&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyM2U5ZGQxOC1kMzI1LWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cOCD4Itd5xZtuL_idaMeDyy4A-2pjD5nQcX7kM35Ac0=&emci=b4b246f5-3c25-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&emdi=23e9dd18-d325-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=954237 "READ NOW")

**RED FLAG #1: Restricted Access to Reproductive Health Care in the U.S.**
**_What's happened?_**

President Trump and his extreme anti-abortion appointees are putting our health and safety at risk. They have launched a coordinated attack to make it harder to access reproductive health care, including emergency abortion care and contraceptive care.

**_Why does it matter?_**

🚩 Need emergency abortion care? The Trump administration has made it clear that they no longer plan to defend pregnant people in medical emergencies—even if your life is at risk.
🚩 Need access to birth control, cancer screenings, or other basic reproductive health care? The Trump administration has frozen funds for these services at many clinics—and yours might be next.
🚩 Serve in the U.S. Military? The Trump administration has made it even harder for you to access abortion care.
🚩 Get care through the Veterans Health Administration? The Trump administration is poised to impose the strictest abortion ban in the country on VA health services.
🚩 Value bodily autonomy? President Trump is laying the groundwork to give embryos legal "rights" to prevent you from making decisions about your own body.

[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106796763/542688208/-1147171705?sourceid=1150618&utm_campaign=25emcus-0401aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=100days&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyM2U5ZGQxOC1kMzI1LWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cOCD4Itd5xZtuL_idaMeDyy4A-2pjD5nQcX7kM35Ac0=&emci=b4b246f5-3c25-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&emdi=23e9dd18-d325-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=954237)
**RED FLAG #2: Cut Public Health Programs and Censored Critical Reproductive Health Information**
**_What's happened?_**

The Trump administration is dismantling key parts of the public health system vital for reproductive care. Indiscriminate funding freezes, mass firings, and the termination of critical research initiatives have hampered the [**Department of Health and Human Services' (HHS)**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106796764/542688211/-1109093640?sourceid=1150618&utm_campaign=25emcus-0401aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=100days&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyM2U5ZGQxOC1kMzI1LWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cOCD4Itd5xZtuL_idaMeDyy4A-2pjD5nQcX7kM35Ac0=&emci=b4b246f5-3c25-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&emdi=23e9dd18-d325-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=954237) essential operations and imperiled domestic reproductive and maternal health programs.

**_Why does it matter?_**

🚩 Need reproductive health care? The Trump administration has decimated the workforce responsible for vital initiatives that are supposed to safeguard your health.
🚩 Pregnant or planning to be? President Trump has shut down the federal data collection system put in place to safeguard your health.
🚩 Rely on IVF to start or grow your family? President Trump has cut off vital research on assisted reproduction.

Trump is unquestionably plotting to take total control of our government — and his quest for a third term is simply the final nail in the coffin of American democracy.
He’s fired inspectors general, FBI agents, and prosecutors who go against his wishes. He’s defying court orders, denying due process and targeting his political enemies with criminal prosecution.
Brick by brick, step by step, he’s dismantling our democracy. Donald Trump does not care if the 2028 election is free and fair. Growing up, I never even dreamed I’d get into politics. I was raised by a single mom in a mobile home park. I watched my mom work hard and complete her teaching degree over nine years while raising us kids.

We lived just a few doors down from my grandmother, who worked into her 70s. I’ll never forget her advice:

**“No matter what work you do, always do more than what they ask of you.”**

I looked to those words as my guide as I worked my way through college and to help lead a major Minnesota manufacturing company.

And I’ve kept that advice in mind during my six plus years in the House representing Minnesota’s 2nd District — successfully capping the cost of insulin at $35 a month for seniors on Medicare.

I’m proud of my record in Congress. But now, I’m ready to take my fight to the Senate, where I can give _all_ Minnesotans a voice.

**It’s never been more important to hold the powerful accountable, folks.**

The Trump administration is running roughshod over the middle class — **working overtime for the drug companies, billionaires and Washington special interests.**

And out-of-control, unelected billionaire Elon Musk is trying to take over our government — and **burn it to the ground.**

Donald Trump is trampling on our rights and freedoms — **as he profits for personal gain.**

And a cowardly Republican Party is rolling over and letting it all happen.

I know I can win this race and help Democrats take back the Senate — but I’ll need your grassroots support. This Senate race could be the most expensive in Minnesota history — and I already hold that record in the House — and **Elon Musk has already pledged a massive $100 million to flip seats like this one.** Election experts are even calling this race a toss-up.

**[We can’t afford for a Republican to win this seat and be a rubber stamp for the destructive MAGA agenda. I was raised by a single mom in a mobile home park. I watched my mom work hard and complete her teaching degree over nine years while raising us kids. We lived just a few doors down from my grandmother, who worked into her 70s. I’ll never forget her advice: “No matter what work you do, always do more than what they ask of you.” I looked to those words as my guide as I worked my way through college and to help lead a major Minnesota manufacturing company. And I’ve kept that advice in mind during my six plus years in the House representing Minnesota’s 2nd District — successfully capping the cost of insulin at $35 a month for seniors on Medicare. I’m proud of my record in Congress. But now, I’m ready to take my fight to the Senate, where I can give all Minnesotans a voice. It’s never been more important to hold the powerful accountable, folks. The Trump administration is running roughshod over the middle class — working overtime for the drug companies, billionaires and Washington special interests. And out-of-control, unelected billionaire Elon Musk is trying to take over our government — and burn it to the ground. Donald Trump is trampling on our rights and freedoms — as he profits for personal gain. And a cowardly Republican Party is rolling over and letting it all happen. I know I can win this race and help Democrats take back the Senate — but I’ll need your grassroots support. This Senate race could be the most expensive in Minnesota history — and I already hold that record in the House — and Elon Musk has already pledged a massive $100 million to flip seats like this one. name: Reid Rasner, CEO
subject: This Isn't the First Crisis. It Won't Be the Last. And That's Okay.
body:
| Hi Peter, If you're feeling uneasy about things right now, you're not alone. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't anxious, too. Markets are volatile, headlines are unnerving, and the future feels uncertain. It's a lot. And yet, when my mind starts to spin, I find some clarity in history. We can learn a great deal from past market crises—what caused them, how investors responded, and the process of recovery that followed. In every case, whenever we thought, "This time is different," we eventually made it through. From the Great Depression to the oil shocks of the '70s, from 9/11 to the financial crisis, from COVID's market freefall to today's geopolitical uncertainty and policy whiplash, investors have faced fear, loss, and doubt time and time again. And still, historically, the long-term trajectory has been growth. In fact, through 13 recessions and 11 bear markets over the last 70 years, U.S. stocks have delivered average annual returns of about 8%.1 That doesn't mean every portfolio follows the same path. And it doesn't mean things aren't painful in the short term. But history reminds us of two things: fear is temporary, and resilience is real.
---
|
---
History gives me hope, but I don't want to oversimplify. Just because markets have always recovered doesn't mean every investor experience is the same, or that every moment of volatility feels manageable while it's happening. Yet, it is noteworthy that we don't help our clients invest based on assumptions that everything will always go up. In fact, we specifically design strategies to include a variety of asset types—some intended to grow, some to preserve, some to help buffer against shocks—because real life is messy, and markets reflect that messiness. No portfolio is perfectly protected from short-term pain. But the goal isn't perfection. It's durability. The work we do with our clients around setting goals, clarifying priorities, and choosing the right mix of investments is a big part of what contributes to long-term resilience. Don't believe us? Check this out:
➜ In early February, Musk’s team laid off 130 staffers at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, or CISA, including 10 regional security specialists who worked with local and state election officials.
➜ Also in February, Attorney General Pam Bondi disbanded a key FBI task force charged with investigating foreign efforts to influence elections.
➜ Bondi has also placed an FBI task force that investigated threats against election workers and polling places on the chopping block, their fate is still up in the air.
➜ In March, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem canceled the funding for national information sharing efforts that helped state and local election officials detect and ward off coordinated hacking attacks and other threats.
This administration has placed a premium on appointing election deniers to positions of power over our elections. From Musk, Noem, and Bondi to FBI Director Kash Patel and the new head of the Department of Justice's Civil Rights division, Harmeet Dhillon, people who spread and defended Trump's "big lie" are in place to wreak havoc on our fundamental right to vote.

The United States has a history of strong preparation and quick work by an information-sharing and analysis network of hundreds of federal, state, and local election, cybersecurity, and law enforcement officials to protect our elections. It's a history we should be proud of.
But now key parts of this security network, much of it built over the past decade, are being systematically dismantled by the Trump administration and Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency, a CNN investigation has found – leaving election offices across the country scrambling to protect against future threats.

body:

#
Friend, Trump was just in Michigan rallying folks to mark his 100 days in office. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106802956/542699611/846650059?refcode=em-4.30.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNmE0N2E5NS1kNjI1LWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zrwN267_V4q0GY13-Z9Y54G0etQO-Ze0lIw3McWZ5eQ=) He got his cheers. He got his headlines. But the truth is, it’s been a chaotic 100 days for the people of Michigan. If he had stepped off that stage and walked a few blocks, he would’ve seen a very different picture of Michigan:
* Moms struggling to afford the basics like groceries and diapers.
* Seniors are terrified that Social Security will be gutted.
* Union workers furious about broken promises and tariffs.

Folks here are stretched thin, frustrated, and looking for someone who’s truly fighting for them. I happen to represent the most competitive district here in America’s swingiest state. We didn’t win by putting on a show. We won by showing up. By listening. By having honest conversations on porches and in churches about what it takes to build a decent life here. As Trump and massive donors like Elon Musk set their sights on this district, they’re hoping money and misinformation will flip this seat. I’m not backing down. Patriot,

I introduced the Military Installation Retail Security Act, a bill that does what should've been done a long time ago:

_**It bans companies owned or controlled by China, Russia, North Korea, or Iran from operating on U.S. military bases.**_

It's unbelievable that the Chinese Communist Party currently owns and operates over 80 stores on our most sensitive military installations, potentially collecting personal data from our troops, including elite units like our Green Berets and Navy SEALs.

**That 's a national security threat hiding in plain sight, and it ends with this bill.**

We owe it to our servicemen and women to protect them from the moment they step onto base. That means locking down their data, cutting off foreign influence, and shutting the door on adversaries who never should've been allowed on our military bases to begin with.

**[This isn’t political. It’s common sense. clean_body: Keep China off our military bases NOW! | Patriot, I introduced the Military Installation Retail Security Act, a bill that does what should've been done a long time ago: It bans companies owned or controlled by China, Russia, North Korea, or Iran from operating on U.S. military bases. It's unbelievable that the Chinese Communist Party currently owns and operates over 80 stores on our most sensitive military installations, potentially collecting personal data from our troops, including elite units like our Green Berets and Navy SEALs. That 's a national security threat hiding in plain sight, and it ends with this bill. We owe it to our servicemen and women to protect them from the moment they step onto base. That means locking down their data, cutting off foreign influence, and shutting the door on adversaries who never should've been allowed on our military bases to begin with. \- Pat Harrigan | Paid for by The Pat Harrigan Committee PO Box 97275, Raleigh, NC 27624 Copyright (C) 2025 Pat Harrigan for Congress, All rights reserved.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Stopping the dumbest trade war in history
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
We still have the rule of law in this country, and Congress must act now.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2533%2E4032634%2EdyuF5d)
---
Today, I’m pushing for a vote in the Senate that would take the blowtorch out of Donald Trump’s hands and strip him of his “emergency” powers he’s using to impose his reckless tariffs. We all know the chaos Trump has already unleashed with his across-the-board tariffs: A plummeting stock market, skyrocketing costs, and mass chaos and confusion. But here’s the thing: Congress has the power to stop this madness by passing my bill today, before more damage is done. Trump has given himself the power to circumvent Congress and declare these tariffs by declaring a state of “emergency”. But Congress can take that power right back by revoking Trump’s fake emergency authority. **That’s why I’m pushing a vote on my bipartisan resolution that would end Trump’s fake emergency authority. I’m calling on every Republican in Congress to stiffen their spines and answer one simple question: Will they stop Trump’s sabotage of our economy? Or will they decide that their entire job is to do nothing but bow down to Donald Trump?** [**I’m fighting my heart out for American families, who are already struggling to make ends meet. Will you chip in whatever you can to support my fight in the Senate to get Republicans to join Democrats and stop Trump’s tariff chaos?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/2990?t=8&akid=2533%2E4032634%2EdyuF5d)

So many people and small businesses are already feeling the economic pain of Trump’s chaotic trade war. Companies like Adidas and Amazon are warning that they’re planning to increase prices for consumers. Americans are bracing to pay higher prices at the grocery store or face empty shelves from supply chain disruptions. Farmers are facing devastating financial losses as countries like China cancel orders of American farming products. Predictions of a tariffs-induced recession as early as this summer are looming. Look, the American economy has taken blow after blow in recent years. | | | Friend, do you remember how it felt when Donald Trump took power in 2017?
We were sad, angry, and hopeless.
But then, we _mobilized_.
**Virginia’s November 2017 House of Delegates elections were one of the first major tests of support for the Trump presidency - and we won _big_.**
I defeated a Republican incumbent as one of 15 red to blue flips.

The House Congressional Review Act (CRA) vote on the California clean cars, trucks, and heavy-duty omnibus waivers will likely take place today. This vote will overturn important clean vehicle standards that cut toxic vehicle emissions. [**Take a second to stand up for our right to clean air by sending your Congressperson a message!**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106807961/542707707/-456362501?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImY3MjVjM2U5LWRiMjUtZjAxMS04YjNkLTYwNDViZGVkOGNjYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=XhQuDc5yrCSyAmt-KXNzTw6RvtMFreONGIoTuw7Sueg=&emci=0ce2043d-1f25-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&emdi=f725c3e9-db25-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=2107230) It's up to us to stop this unprecedented and reckless attack on the Clean Air Act — through a rollback on Clean Vehicle Waivers — and state rights. This comes down to yet another attack on our science based environmental policies and on state rights. ### MassGOP Demands Answers About State Budget's $5 Million Immigrant Legal Defense Fund and Bill for Illegal Immigrants Facing Deportation
---
---
| BOSTON, MA -- On Tuesday, State House Democrats passed a $5 million provision in the FY26 budget setting aside $5 million for the implementation of an "immigration legal services program" curiously similar to one filed earlier this year that would provide illegal immigrants facing deportation with taxpayer-funded defense lawyers.
The line item, rolled into Section 2 and 3 of the House Ways and Means Budget and presented by Chair Aaron Michlewitz (D-Boston) earlier this month, would allocate an additional $500,000 to the state Office of Refugees of Immigrants (ORI) to dispense grants to "designated non-profit organizations to increase access legal representation for immigrants and refugees in the commonwealth, including, but not limited to, legal assistance in a single consultation or ongoing legal representation and all legal advice, advocacy and related assistance."
In February, Democratic Reps. David Rogers (D-Cambridge) and Frank Moran (D-Lawrence) presented standalone legislation that would give additional funds to ORI so that it may "grant funds to qualified immigration legal service providers and the nonprofit organizations and law firms who employ them to provide no-cost legal defense to eligible low-income immigrants." No dollar amount was presented at the time.
In Rogers's own words, given the presence of federal authorities arresting dangerous illegal immigrants in Massachusetts "it is all the more crucial to protect the rights of those who arrive in this country looking to build a better life."
The MassGOP vigorously opposes this provision and thanks Rep. Marc Lombardo (R-Billerica) and the entire Republican House caucus for bringing it to the attention of the public.
"It is unconscionable that taxpayers will be forced to pay the legal bills for illegal immigrants facing removal orders. Beacon Hill Democrats have gone so far left that they simply don't represent the hardworking taxpayers anymore. This line item makes this budget vote an easy 'No,'" said Rep. Lombardo.

BACKGROUND:
Line item 4003-0124 in Section 2 and 3 of the FY2026 state budget tasks ORI with distributing $500,000 in taxpayer dollars to provide "legal assistance in a single consultation or ongoing legal representation and all legal advice, advocacy and related assistance" to immigrants without specifying whether or not they have legal status or face deportation. ([Ways & Means Final Budget](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001YKHp29f5EoOxRoTpYYCQkuNeDlkwwjNEL-NxgD84xe5VDyg0RfaVKo8HQUfivMwobCamSK22KUaak8VrR3YyXAPf6nJ1EK8hEIfE9SRyqU_tcw3ZYsSdp_RilHbRCAe60KS5AvJKx40mHnLhl34SZsDKUpTGU5vL_NF_zFIocQhSpKzhCQzEgTF-W3clkZDO5kNKAw3B6f5ibRu75MClbnx3qabyqIwkaJflEjsGOHMnlX26BnSpaw==&c=Itj7XGWy3A0OM3m-mLkIx0WNSlyuDaWxi7MDg29c7r6x-8kDJ9CJzQ==&ch=UszVkmWV56ImjfVyF_HckxhfpY29EuqNW_6bz9cVWtXJH58nF2I9MQ==), Section 2 & 3, Page 78, 4/10/25)
In February, Democratic lawmakers introduced H.1954 to provide taxpayer-funded legal services to illegal immigrants facing deportation. ([MA Legislature](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001YKHp29f5EoOxRoTpYYCQkuNeDlkwwjNEL-NxgD84xe5VDyg0RfaVKo8HQUfivMwoWd4M0W2Hiv4RfE-lURu9exBrhLP-uLu582zGVIch9eY8UEqTJJKLJGWQFIzD0qlAwM5r077GNLr4eYqT6PSBXcaMypJpl1xZwNvx1dCvuj06vqN2SRB3mQ==&c=Itj7XGWy3A0OM3m-mLkIx0WNSlyuDaWxi7MDg29c7r6x-8kDJ9CJzQ==&ch=UszVkmWV56ImjfVyF_HckxhfpY29EuqNW_6bz9cVWtXJH58nF2I9MQ==), 2/27/25)

clean_body: | | | | | | | == | MassGOP Demands Answers About State Budget's $5 Million Immigrant Legal Defense Fund and Bill for Illegal Immigrants Facing Deportation | BOSTON, MA -- On Tuesday, State House Democrats passed a $5 million provision in the FY26 budget setting aside $5 million for the implementation of an "immigration legal services program" curiously similar to one filed earlier this year that would provide illegal immigrants facing deportation with taxpayer-funded defense lawyers. The line item, rolled into Section 2 and 3 of the House Ways and Means Budget and presented by Chair Aaron Michlewitz (D-Boston) earlier this month, would allocate an additional $500,000 to the state Office of Refugees of Immigrants (ORI) to dispense grants to "designated non-profit organizations to increase access legal representation for immigrants and refugees in the commonwealth, including, but not limited to, legal assistance in a single consultation or ongoing legal representation and all legal advice, advocacy and related assistance." In February, Democratic Reps. David Rogers (D-Cambridge) and Frank Moran (D-Lawrence) presented standalone legislation that would give additional funds to ORI so that it may "grant funds to qualified immigration legal service providers and the nonprofit organizations and law firms who employ them to provide no-cost legal defense to eligible low-income immigrants." No dollar amount was presented at the time. In Rogers's own words, given the presence of federal authorities arresting dangerous illegal immigrants in Massachusetts "it is all the more crucial to protect the rights of those who arrive in this country looking to build a better life." The MassGOP vigorously opposes this provision and thanks Rep. Marc Lombardo (R-Billerica) and the entire Republican House caucus for bringing it to the attention of the public. "It is unconscionable that taxpayers will be forced to pay the legal bills for illegal immigrants facing removal orders. Beacon Hill Democrats have gone so far left that they simply don't represent the hardworking taxpayers anymore. This line item makes this budget vote an easy 'No,'" said Rep. Lombardo. BACKGROUND: Line item 4003-0124 in Section 2 and 3 of the FY2026 state budget tasks ORI with distributing $500,000 in taxpayer dollars to provide "legal assistance in a single consultation or ongoing legal representation and all legal advice, advocacy and related assistance" to immigrants without specifying whether or not they have legal status or face deportation. (==, Section 2 & 3, Page 78, 4/10/25) In February, Democratic lawmakers introduced H.1954 to provide taxpayer-funded legal services to illegal immigrants facing deportation. (==, 2/27/25) Rep. Rogers, a sponsor of H.1954, called his bill "crucial" in a newsletter to supporters. Peter, we must confront the fact that our great country is going through a generational regression.
Misinformation, disinformation, and injustice loom over society like a dark cloud. The rule of law and fundamental fairness are at risk. Governing norms have been needlessly cast aside. Compassion in our government is in short supply.
**In this time of maximum danger to our country, all who love America most dearly must stand up and speak out for the principles that, at our best, define the nation.**
As I reflect on our current challenges, I am reminded of a critical moment in a turbulent era of our nation's history:
On June 11, 1963, the Deputy Attorney General, Nicholas Katzenbach, peacefully escorted James Hood and my late sister-in-law Vivian Malone onto campus as they integrated the University of Alabama, past Governor Wallace's infamous blockade.
That evening, President Kennedy addressed the American people not merely about a political disagreement, but about a profound moral reckoning for our republic. Every single word rang with conviction and moral clarity, making the case and pointing the way toward what would become the signature achievements of the Civil Rights Era and the foundation of modern America.
Today, our current moment presents both possibility and peril for the fundamental freedoms and pro-democracy principles we hold dear.
**It is in these extraordinary moments — these complex and contradictory chapters in the life of our nation — and through the work of ordinary yet extraordinary people that America's character is revealed, and our future determined.**
Right now, the progress we have made as a nation — long sought and long fought for — is being dismantled right before our very eyes.
We see it in House Republicans passing the extreme SAVE Act, which could disenfranchise millions of Americans. We see it in North Carolina, where Republican Jefferson Griffin is attempting to steal a seat on that state's highest court. We see it in relentless GOP efforts to gerrymander districts across the country, silencing the voices of millions.
But make no mistake: there is still reason for hope.
Just look at Wisconsin, where ordinary yet extraordinary people — who suffered under years of illegitimate minority rule amid ruthless gerrymandering — kept pressing forward for a truly representative democracy.
At the NDRC, we’ve been proud to fight by their side. After years of steadfast work, the people of Wisconsin finally won a pro-democracy majority on the state supreme court that helped deliver fair maps — which meant a fair chance for all Wisconsinites to be heard. And earlier this month, we were proud to work alongside them as they protected that majority by electing Justice Susan Crawford to the Wisconsin Supreme Court.

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for re-election so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in the United States Senate. The Radical Left has him circled as a prime target to defeat in the 2026 Midterm Elections. Can he count on your support? _

body:
Here’s my story
[ ](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=d0460b05335249d987e24cbe9172f46e&_e=lM7uifjhhD7vD3ciC9ALp4cZALxICfwSAFrPXnhU5vlnwyr-macwoYi68BBFm8K0QQ4d1BflJFa8q-x3icJQFBPjvXqRuL2c9NEIldXiOBkXYVeuj3oQbrYimemQ9rwuX-tH6n_RDha_NrpXFTT0z973DSK8pkpPH0fs-L2pjlMSz6BfM1F7zO7mAlB9xpjl_E3B8utpuglhSXkydQDmdpzGkJxmq8Lic6xvztCpHgIgdpKNRv12_LwJ77krlSHC54eL06eLebwZEIm5gqG7PqpBVPj0GkUQZyUN41QXYUgb8ePUmq-hJgvFLfrB6zZDMR8UhPjhXZfaUnuO99QQhH1o266gJPeqIh14BqHYiWifeQRaybJ6RFj5BOO2sUGN)
Fellow Patriot,
Hi! My name is Alea.
I was born in Toledo, Ohio to an American mother and an Iraqi father - I know - an unusual combination. When you are a kid, you don’t know where your parents are from, but you just know they are your parents. I was a normal kid, went to school, ate McDonalds, and spent weekends with my grandparents.
[ ](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=d0460b05335249d987e24cbe9172f46e&_e=lM7uifjhhD7vD3ciC9ALp4cZALxICfwSAFrPXnhU5vlnwyr-macwoYi68BBFm8K0QQ4d1BflJFa8q-x3icJQFBPjvXqRuL2c9NEIldXiOBkXYVeuj3oQbrYimemQ9rwuX-tH6n_RDha_NrpXFTT0z973DSK8pkpPH0fs-L2pjlMSz6BfM1F7zO7mAlB9xpjl_E3B8utpuglhSXkydQDmdpzGkJxmq8Lic6xvztCpHgKK3Hqb6LaxT-cPa1czr2ZYxGPXal7MSoXgasTYc-O9_Tu-vg3TtnRZzoHHuTcVOqGUmLjRI9hMi3NYueL4NhzrBLHtJAovgaKfpm9kaaWaQUGnlBAd-dhLj-6yclFBjksTPwsk9N7gYpvuuePeTXZe)
At the age of eight, I was kidnapped to Iraq, unfortunately by my own father. My life has never been the same, but believe it or not, it made me who I am today.
**Being kidnapped and losing my freedom is what made me appreciate the freedoms so many in the U.S. take for granted. I know firsthand what it’s like to lose your freedom – and was forced to live under Saddam Hussein’s brutal and repressive regime in Iraq, where being a woman means having no rights, speaking out costs you your life, and your future is not your own.**
[ **_I want to tell you about myself and my story, and I hope that after reading this, you’ll consider supporting my campaign for Congress to defeat one of the most vulnerable Democrats in America and advance President Trump’s America First policies._** ](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=d0460b05335249d987e24cbe9172f46e&_e=lM7uifjhhD7vD3ciC9ALp4cZALxICfwSAFrPXnhU5vlnwyr-macwoYi68BBFm8K0QQ4d1BflJFa8q-x3icJQFBPjvXqRuL2c9NEIldXiOBkXYVeuj3oQbrYimemQ9rwuX-tH6n_RDha_NrpXFTT0z973DSK8pkpPH0fs-L2pjlMSz6BfM1F7zO7mAlB9xpjl_E3B8utpuglhSXkydQDmdpzGkJxmq8Lic6xvztCpHgIJcqKb0QgZfLbMIAj67hOfZQyadqQYOM8kscIh0ZDKDanEu11PIYm1pj58EgSHqkbZpPKVvYH3xETbZQbLX9n76_bvyJt3tzjx0kT2Ei1Xa2NG2ZrDYEavVFM6JEeh6UfAGKSAVOl9MoYmCgupDHT3)
When I was 8 and my sister was 3, we took a family trip with my parents to visit my father’s mother who was sick in Iraq. At first, it was a wonderful experience meeting family for the first time. **_But my entire world would soon change forever._**
The night before our flight back to America, my dad woke us up for a surprise trip to my aunt’s house for ice cream and candy. As any little kid would, we relished the excitement of being up past our bed time, playing after we had our fill of sweets. **But we soon realized both of our parents were nowhere to be found._That’s when my nightmare began._**
Hours that felt like months and several nights of crying myself to sleep passed before they returned. Our family members they left us with didn’t speak English and we didn’t speak Arabic.
When they finally did return, it wasn’t the happy reunion I hoped for. My father had given my mother a heartbreaking ultimatum: She could only take one of us back to America. Fearing for my sister who was only 3 years old, my mother made an impossible decision, and **I was left behind.**
As a young girl, I had no choice but to adjust to my new life.
I learned Arabic and went to school. My family helped me and tried to comfort me as much as possible. I was surrounded by good people in Mosul, _but I never stopped trying to get back to America–back to my home._
Following Operation Desert Storm, U.S. forces protected the civilian population in northern Iraq. I remember a U.S. helicopter landing near my home in Mosul. I desperately begged the aircrew to take me back home. Of course, they couldn’t, but I never lost sight of my goal – not once during my four years in Iraq.
**Neither did my mother.** I didn’t know this then, but she was working with the FBI and local government officials in Toledo to secure my return home. My father was arrested for kidnapping, and the court told him he could not be released until I was brought back to the United States.
Finally, **I was reunited with my mother and my life in Ohio.** I was 12 years old, and a lot changed since I was last in America. I spoke broken English and was behind academically. It was a tough road, but I made it slowly.
[ ](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=d0460b05335249d987e24cbe9172f46e&_e=lM7uifjhhD7vD3ciC9ALp4cZALxICfwSAFrPXnhU5vlnwyr-macwoYi68BBFm8K0QQ4d1BflJFa8q-x3icJQFBPjvXqRuL2c9NEIldXiOBkXYVeuj3oQbrYimemQ9rwuX-tH6n_RDha_NrpXFTT0z973DSK8pkpPH0fs-L2pjlMSz6BfM1F7zO7mAlB9xpjl_E3B8utpuglhSXkydQDmdpzGkJxmq8Lic6xvztCpHgLYOpU8eowUlqX7miBUumJlNSIf5iiugO1XpRgdb9yvVYrW5VFzWDjjDXHb5uj2m5TJAmUZ7gLCnvHpLQir4GUVHM2CdAVdvoH5InaMV6cOZqY9Zkrfwv_09VKaPAhvFvM5Bzn49FOoxTh7k51j7mQ1)
As a junior in high school, I watched in horror as our country was attacked on September 11, 2001. I knew I had to do something – to lead by example and show my fellow Americans that, in fact, Arab Americans love our country – and to give back to the country that gave me a chance.
**So, I walked into an Air Force recruiting office and asked to do whatever job deployed the most.**
A year later, I was in basic training, learning to become an Airman.
[ ](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=d0460b05335249d987e24cbe9172f46e&_e=lM7uifjhhD7vD3ciC9ALp4cZALxICfwSAFrPXnhU5vlnwyr-macwoYi68BBFm8K0QQ4d1BflJFa8q-x3icJQFBPjvXqRuL2c9NEIldXiOBkXYVeuj3oQbrYimemQ9rwuX-tH6n_RDha_NrpXFTT0z973DSK8pkpPH0fs-L2pjlMSz6BfM1F7zO7mAlB9xpjl_E3B8utpuglhSXkydQDmdpzGkJxmq8Lic6xvztCpHgJsQFeRIFpcBg16Oruxyf8kXb9t2BZsG68jnGQCbTFYQNh5vqtULzx3uAHPnchHfNhN6sC474sLfMLjFEiHqx7Y2T-KI1ySM51lWOzMxjYF_xol-8HfOzuNIrvbxXAgytDMAMrHGvBqN4-HjyhGq7mz)
Since then, I’ve spent my career in military intelligence, serving both active duty and in the Air Force Reserve. Today I’m a Lieutenant Colonel. I’ve advised top military leaders, deployed to the Middle East, and used my experience to help America understand the culture and geopolitics of Iraq and Syria.
**America gave me a second chance, and I am committed to continuing my service to this country with everything I have.** [ That's why I decided to run for Congress - and I hope I can count on your support. ](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=d0460b05335249d987e24cbe9172f46e&_e=lM7uifjhhD7vD3ciC9ALp4cZALxICfwSAFrPXnhU5vlnwyr-macwoYi68BBFm8K0QQ4d1BflJFa8q-x3icJQFBPjvXqRuL2c9NEIldXiOBkXYVeuj3oQbrYimemQ9rwuX-tH6n_RDha_NrpXFTT0z973DSK8pkpPH0fs-L2pjlMSz6BfM1F7zO7mAlB9xpjl_E3B8utpuglhSXkydQDmdpzGkJxmq8Lic6xvztCpHgKdJ_yQ9sEA5rz3gG4OKXIWOeczdJ8cBQgSJStF-2zD_LEHUe0kU6XK547ibvUyHgTtIaemzGSvqJbS9pHDXYpUGi7NfgpzvHP57UOTXI9LoyeIZ-mbLB4H7EKxODCdr1JmgoRoHa2JcmxTFk6FdyQM)
**My experiences have taught me that freedom isn’t free, and you never know what you had until you lose it.** America needs strong leaders who understand that and who will stand up to ensure that future generations have a stronger, better, freer country than we inherited.
Our military, our families, and our freedoms are worth fighting for. And I will never stop fighting for you and I will always put America First. I hope you will join me on this mission.
With deep gratitude,
Alea Nadeem
Candidate for U.S. Congress

When I was 8 and my sister was 3, we took a family trip with my parents to visit my father’s mother who was sick in Iraq. At first, it was a wonderful experience meeting family for the first time. But my entire world would soon change forever. The night before our flight back to America, my dad woke us up for a surprise trip to my aunt’s house for ice cream and candy. As any little kid would, we relished the excitement of being up past our bed time, playing after we had our fill of sweets. But we soon realized both of our parents were nowhere to be found.That’s when my nightmare began. Hours that felt like months and several nights of crying myself to sleep passed before they returned. Our family members they left us with didn’t speak English and we didn’t speak Arabic. When they finally did return, it wasn’t the happy reunion I hoped for. My father had given my mother a heartbreaking ultimatum: She could only take one of us back to America. Fearing for my sister who was only 3 years old, my mother made an impossible decision, and I was left behind. As a young girl, I had no choice but to adjust to my new life. I learned Arabic and went to school. My family helped me and tried to comfort me as much as possible. I was surrounded by good people in Mosul, but I never stopped trying to get back to America–back to my home. Following Operation Desert Storm, U.S. forces protected the civilian population in northern Iraq. I remember a U.S. helicopter landing near my home in Mosul. I desperately begged the aircrew to take me back home. Of course, they couldn’t, but I never lost sight of my goal – not once during my four years in Iraq. Neither did my mother. I didn’t know this then, but she was working with the FBI and local government officials in Toledo to secure my return home. My father was arrested for kidnapping, and the court told him he could not be released until I was brought back to the United States. Finally, I was reunited with my mother and my life in Ohio. I was 12 years old, and a lot changed since I was last in America. I spoke broken English and was behind academically. It was a tough road, but I made it slowly. As a junior in high school, I watched in horror as our country was attacked on September 11, 2001. I knew I had to do something – to lead by example and show my fellow Americans that, in fact, Arab Americans love our country – and to give back to the country that gave me a chance. So, I walked into an Air Force recruiting office and asked to do whatever job deployed the most. A year later, I was in basic training, learning to become an Airman. Since then, I’ve spent my career in military intelligence, serving both active duty and in the Air Force Reserve. Today I’m a Lieutenant Colonel. I’ve advised top military leaders, deployed to the Middle East, and used my experience to help America understand the culture and geopolitics of Iraq and Syria. America gave me a second chance, and I am committed to continuing my service to this country with everything I have. My experiences have taught me that freedom isn’t free, and you never know what you had until you lose it. America needs strong leaders who understand that and who will stand up to ensure that future generations have a stronger, better, freer country than we inherited. Our military, our families, and our freedoms are worth fighting for. And I will never stop fighting for you and I will always put America First. I hope you will join me on this mission. With deep gratitude, Alea Nadeem Candidate for U.S. Congress Paid for by Alea for Congress **The appearance of Alea Nadeem in military uniform does not imply or constitute endorsement by the U.S. Air Force or U.S. Department of Defense.

Peter,

Quite a bit has happened in the past month...

- The DNC has vowed to pour millions of dollars into state parties including Texas.
- A liberal organization called ‘Contest Every Race’ is vowing to do just that with millions invested in rural areas like we have here in Texas.
- And the DCCC continued its torrid fundraising pace and is currently sitting on more than $33 million that they plan to spend in districts President Trump won by more than 15 points, just like this one.

If you need more convincing, here are a few things worth highlighting about Marlene and our race:
1. **DCCC calls Arizona’s 1st Congressional District a “district in play.”** Our time is now to take back the House majority and unseat David Schweikert for his poor leadership. This race will be extremely competitive, but with your support, _we can win._
2. **David Schweikert is hiding from his constituents.** Threats to our economic security and access to lifesaving healthcare have not gone unnoticed by the people of AZ-01. When given the opportunity to speak directly to Arizonans in the CD1 Townhall _just last week_ , Schweikert was nowhere to be found. AZ-01 deserves leadership that will show up to hear their concerns.
3. **Our democracy and institutions are under attack, and Schweikert is not only letting it happen but voting for the very policies that have put so many Arizonan families at risk.** Schweikert voted for the budget blueprint that would pave the way to gut Social Security and Medicaid. _He is not on our side._
4. **Marlene will put Arizona families first.** As the daughter of Cuban immigrants and mother of five children, family means everything to Marlene. She will fight for the families of Arizona and prioritize the issues affecting them. Trump’s tariffs and Musk’s dangerous DOGE agenda are hurting a lot of our neighbors. Marlene is ready to stand up to the recklessness of this administration.

Marlene’s campaign is our best shot at unseating David Schweikert, but we must continue showing early grassroots support behind our movement.

Jason Crow For Congress [https://nvlupin.blob.core.windows.net/images/van/NGP/NGP21/1/88523/images/logoJC%20(1).png]
Team,

Across the country, Donald Trump and his extreme Republican enablers are working to divide us and undermine the very foundation of our democracy.

They want to help the rich get richer and close the doors to freedom and opportunity that have made America a beacon of hope for centuries.

This moment isn’t just about resisting extremism, it’s about fighting for a positive vision for our future.

The America I’m fighting for is one where everyone has a fair shot to work hard and get ahead, where our differences make us stronger, and where we build a better tomorrow together — because that’s what Coloradans do.

To do this requires that we elect leaders who embody “servant leadership.” I talk a lot about this concept — the notion that every leader should consider themselves a servant of the people that they are leading.

I told the New York Times last month, “You need to have the right people of integrity, servant leaders who understand their communities, who are respected by their communities. ”

Those are the leaders I’m working to elect in Colorado and across the country. Leaders who will serve their community with integrity and grit, and who aren’t afraid to take on the toughest fights.

Your support now will help me embody those values in Congress — and will help me elect leaders who share these values, too. Will you pitch in today to support my campaign and help fight for what we believe in? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc-em-apr25]

Hey Peter, it’s Becca. **Breaking news: My team just got word that Mohsen Mahdawi — a Vermont resident who was wrongfully arrested by ICE agents — has been released on bail. Today’s news shows us what we can do when we fight for justice, when we come together and use our voices.** Last night, I led a rally to demand the immediate release of Mohsen Mahdawi. I was so proud to see so many people join us to call attention to this injustice — and I’m even more proud to see that our voices have had an impact. Let this moment inspire us to keep up the fight. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106820838/542735922/-1865709748?refcode=AU_RAB_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20250430_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ODg3ZTZhOS1lNjI1LWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iLqVd7NMHbD674ys8iQS8mx-piwZ-3w_ztMwBygo2LA=) This is a major win for our cause — but this fight is far from over. The Trump administration is disappearing people in this country under the guise of “immigration reform” and “safety.” **It’s inhumane and _a total and blatant violation of the Constitution._** Mohsen Mahdawi and countless others are being attacked because of free speech. This should terrify every single person living in this country, regardless of your citizenship status. If the Trump Administration can come for one of us, they can come for all of us. Friend,

Today is the day. At midnight, our campaign’s first end-of-month fundraising deadline hits, marking one full month since I relaunched my run for Congress in NV-03.

We’re so close to our $5,000 goal, but we need one final push to get there—[**and I’m counting on YOU.**](http://links.martynevada.com/u/click?_t=3a5223257aca4a93ac027b228c2c976d&_m=319636cd56b0469488ad2a4f454964a8&_e=mI9DGX_K2wV_8IYCnvNA9ijsDBvs93Nmm8AWq4qJ2WreABh9uhXluYbJVy3jZBMvo4j8AjIzWmOFhGdfooRu-qylLfplukCWR97NnJLSbkjiVXscAIPogegXtUhWicAQi7pnPHF5jJbYhaUVa7LQyBB38ZuX_taKvnzUhJJI1yJBWAukFbNBGG6oprTQ1pVvwUXoa3-uHAJtzIg_kl6D0E0zu73CV6NFrwI0AW-CsTuue8FuWxIt8Uf_75EE9UN8xWKSVF3-9qicGJfZY6id5PY5Vg-WfnJa8OOIDK-g-egEnguNmrRHJQef4N1tXKTKZD0-ErZ1jJfhcTuJPGtcmaKQeaqY4pCf6dxIE3gUTy9POkNhzY64KNY7BwOTvI0vElVQQ_dbiFeEnMIbS-dx-TScwv1b2GXmvE5nCQcrHpM%3D)

This swing district is a battleground, and every dollar we raise today will help us compete, spread our message, and flip this seat.

We’re fighting for secure borders, a strong economy, and an America First agenda. But I can’t do it alone. [** _Rush Before Midnight »_ **](http://links.martynevada.com/u/click?_t=3a5223257aca4a93ac027b228c2c976d&_m=319636cd56b0469488ad2a4f454964a8&_e=mI9DGX_K2wV_8IYCnvNA9ijsDBvs93Nmm8AWq4qJ2WreABh9uhXluYbJVy3jZBMvo4j8AjIzWmOFhGdfooRu-qylLfplukCWR97NnJLSbkjiVXscAIPogegXtUhWicAQi7pnPHF5jJbYhaUVa7LQyBB38ZuX_taKvnzUhJJI1yJBWAukFbNBGG6oprTQ1pVvwUXoa3-uHAJtzIg_kl6D0E0zu73CV6NFrwI0AW-CsTuue8FuWxIt8Uf_75EE9UN8_voK2Y_t3qXWZS8Si4iYvHEkySqVSs-hkU1IiVbnQwHtNg9jLoF43_KbBpti6-Ld0IAUiBBM4QPHrwyj_bY_GjP5UnxE7g4o5RhJaBML7uPoIROYxIJTUkTTdPMo8BA6pT2T2Z3tX7WCanhIU9y9aU-4eFJg52hR9Ey3sEXc2vI%3D)

Don’t wait—the clock is ticking. [**Donate now and let’s make this deadline a win!**](http://links.martynevada.com/u/click?_t=3a5223257aca4a93ac027b228c2c976d&_m=319636cd56b0469488ad2a4f454964a8&_e=mI9DGX_K2wV_8IYCnvNA9ijsDBvs93Nmm8AWq4qJ2WreABh9uhXluYbJVy3jZBMvo4j8AjIzWmOFhGdfooRu-qylLfplukCWR97NnJLSbkjiVXscAIPogegXtUhWicAQi7pnPHF5jJbYhaUVa7LQyBB38ZuX_taKvnzUhJJI1yJBWAukFbNBGG6oprTQ1pVvwUXoa3-uHAJtzIg_kl6D0E0zu73CV6NFrwI0AW-CsTuue8FuWxIt8Uf_75EE9UN84pnooZ8kcxuRkhZB2b9-Ss-kJ0IWQnLrashNL9TH4BEihbfIFXpPmcngO0avqpQn4wtDX8Fnj3fhF5Q4mDLFfYGLlzFwSOfZLK2HuMUOH2SKkOJccAjGahGrdH_iUHJJfwIxrJblfVkKAj3NbMp_X9RdoiBovtKR5e7cU2SXDn0%3D) Finish the Fight!

| **ABOUT MARTY**
**Marty O’Donnell isn’t a politician** and he’s not taking any corporate PAC money. Marty will give us a voice – not special interests or Wall Street. It’s time to turn our nation around to make life better for Nevadans.

**Marty O’Donnell has an ear for solving problems.** He’s an award-winning composer who wrote the iconic soundtracks for the video games Halo and Destiny. Marty will cut through the noise in DC.

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Donavan McKinney is running for Congress in Michigan’s 13th district, and
we’re proud to have endorsed him as Justice Democrats’ first 2026
candidate.

Here’s the truth: his opponent, Rep. Shri Thanedar, has got to go.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20250430-1-dm?refcode=em20250430-36628&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36628_1203867_MDkm4L&akid=36628%2E1203867%2EMDkm4L ]A picture of Shri Thandedar sitting in a plane.

Thanedar is a flip-flopper and a political opportunist. He ran as a
progressive because it was convenient, but not because he genuinely shares
our values. He’s even considered switching parties.

In fact, Thanedar went from a candidate AIPAC once spent against to one
they now proudly support. He’s taken AIPAC-sponsored trips to Israel and
refused to support the only bill calling for a permanent ceasefire in
Gaza. In Congress, he’s voted in lockstep with the pro-Israel lobby –
abandoning the values of peace and justice.

Thanedar will never fight for the working class because he is not part of
it. He’s a multimillionaire businessman who bought his way into office
using his personal wealth to fund his campaigns. He doesn’t understand the
need for things like Medicare for All, fighting for Social Security and
Medicaid, and taking on corporate lobbies like Big Crypto because he is
simply out of touch with the people he’s supposed to represent. While
Thanedar is Detroit’s own Elon Musk, Donavan is running for this seat
because he’s not a millionaire or billionaire.

To make matters worse, Thanedar is just bad at being a Congressman. His
office has been plagued with accusations of poor constituent services and
he was even sued for fraud. The people of Detroit and the rest of MI-13
deserve better.

That’s where Donavan comes in. He’s a lifelong Detroiter who’s always
stood up for progressive values – not just when it’s convenient for him.
While billionaires and corporate interests tear our government apart, we
need a working-class champion like Donavan, not another multimillionaire
like Thanedar.

to help us reach our $50,000 goal and kickstart this race with a surge of
grassroots support?

name: Derek Tran
subject: Remembering 50 years since the fall of Saigon.
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106824918/542744997/2039042026?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTAxMjY2ODgtZWIyNS1mMDExLThiM2QtNjA0NWJkZWQ4Y2NhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ONX9N8BvF1SiR1JC9sw5fB6Mclyc0sdqQNCyUAsPptY=)
Today marks 50 years since the Fall of Saigon -- a day we know as Black April. It’s a day of mourning and profound loss, but also a reminder of what we carry with us: resilience, duty, and the hope of a better future.

Over 500,000 perished at sea trying to escape in the aftermath. Black April honors their memories, as well as the sacrifice of more than 58,000 American service members and 260,000 South Vietnamese soldiers who fought for freedom.

My father was one of the boat people. After the South fell in 1975, he fled Vietnam with his wife and children. Their boat capsized and he lost everything -- his wife, two sons, and two daughters. Only he and three of my half-sisters survived. But he didn’t give up.

He made it to a refugee camp in Indonesia and eventually to the United States. That’s where I was born -- in Monterey Park, California.

Who I am today is shaped by the journey my parents took to give me this chance. They never let me forget how lucky we were or how important it was that we give back.

**That’s why I enlisted in the Army at 18. It’s why I became a lawyer to fight for workers, immigrants, and survivors. And it’s why I ran for Congress: to serve the country that gave my family a second chance, and ensure that chance still exists for others.**

Today, we honored the generations who rose from our struggle and gave back to this country. This is especially important given everything happening in Washington. Extremists in power are pushing immigrants away, fueling division, and trying to erase who we are.

I didn’t come to Washington to play politics. I came to fight for families like mine, for veterans, for workers, for every person trying to build a life with dignity.

Fifty years after the Fall of Saigon, I’m serving in Congress because my community believed in something better. That’s the story I carry. And that’s what I’m here to protect.

clean_body: | = Today marks 50 years since the Fall of Saigon -- a day we know as Black April. It’s a day of mourning and profound loss, but also a reminder of what we carry with us: resilience, duty, and the hope of a better future. Over 500,000 perished at sea trying to escape in the aftermath. Black April honors their memories, as well as the sacrifice of more than 58,000 American service members and 260,000 South Vietnamese soldiers who fought for freedom. My father was one of the boat people. After the South fell in 1975, he fled Vietnam with his wife and children. Their boat capsized and he lost everything -- his wife, two sons, and two daughters. Only he and three of my half-sisters survived. But he didn’t give up. He made it to a refugee camp in Indonesia and eventually to the United States. That’s where I was born -- in Monterey Park, California. Who I am today is shaped by the journey my parents took to give me this chance. They never let me forget how lucky we were or how important it was that we give back. That’s why I enlisted in the Army at 18. It’s why I became a lawyer to fight for workers, immigrants, and survivors. And it’s why I ran for Congress: to serve the country that gave my family a second chance, and ensure that chance still exists for others. Today, we honored the generations who rose from our struggle and gave back to this country. This is especially important given everything happening in Washington. Extremists in power are pushing immigrants away, fueling division, and trying to erase who we are. I didn’t come to Washington to play politics. I came to fight for families like mine, for veterans, for workers, for every person trying to build a life with dignity. Fifty years after the Fall of Saigon, I’m serving in Congress because my community believed in something better. That’s the story I carry. And that’s what I’m here to protect. Thank you for believing in this work. Dear Derek,
Tomorrow is my governor campaign’s second ever fundraising deadline, and a lot’s on the line.
**[So I’m writing to you directly to ask if you’ll donate $5 or whatever you can spare to help us reach our $75,000 email end-of-month fundraising goal?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250430_1_ak?refcode=em20250430-39686&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39686_3422442_ZDkqMV&akid=39686%2E3422442%2EZDkqMV)**
Early fundraising has a lot of upsides. It can help us raise more money, by showing people that this is a campaign to take seriously. It can send a message to special interests that they should stay out of this race. And perhaps most importantly, it gives us the ability to better plan our resources and stretch our donations the furthest they can go.
I know that many political campaigns go overboard with their fundraising asks. I stay very mindful of this—and at the very least, I try to keep things fun and informational, so you can get a laugh and learn a thing or two.
But because I reject money from corporations, lobbyists, and executives at Big Pharma, Big Oil, and Big Banks, the only way I can raise the resources I need to win and keep fighting for working people is through grassroots donations.
**[Ahead of our April fundraising deadline tomorrow, I’m asking you personally: will you chip in $5 or more to help our campaign get off to the strongest possible start?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250430_1_ak?refcode=em20250430-39686&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39686_3422442_ZDkqMV&akid=39686%2E3422442%2EZDkqMV)**

Fellow American,

Growing up in Central, South Carolina, I watched my parents run our family's restaurant, liquor store, and pool hall. They stayed connected to our community by listening to their customers' perspectives. Those conversations taught me the value of respecting diverse opinions, even when they differ from my own--a principle we need more of today.

body:
Help me commemorate his first 100 days in office.
| Peter,
---
President Trump is about to officially mark his first 100 days in office!
---
**Those first 100 days in office have been nothing short of an incredible success for the American people.**
---
From securing our border to draining the Swamp, he’s made great strides towards restoring America’s former glory and ushering in a new “golden age” for our country.

**As a doctor, I know how important access to affordable healthcare is.** In Adams County, 65% of my patients' families were on Medicaid – but still struggling to make ends meet. disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
It might seem like everything is spinning out of control right now, but the truth continues to be the truth. So, here’s a reality check:
#

Friends —
After a pretty insane first hundred days of Trump’s presidency, we’re coming up on our end of month deadline tonight.
It might seem like everything is spinning out of control right now, but the truth continues to be the truth. So, here’s a reality check:
Due process is real, and everyone in the United States is entitled to it.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the land, and whether you agree or not, they make the final decision on whether something is constitutional or not.
Blanket, across-the-board tariffs are bad policy — they’ll raise prices on American families, and they’re even worse when you do it alone and don’t coordinate on a united front with your allies.
And, for that matter, the United States is at its best when we work with our allies — democracies that share our values, not oligarchies and autocracies that repress civil rights and restrict the power of the people.
**That’s the truth.**
That’s what Mark believes. That’s what most Americans (still) believe. And when we’re on the other side of Trump, that’s what we’re going to get back to.
But, until then, we have to continue speaking out. We have to take action when we can, where we can. We have to defend our communities and our values. And we’ve got to support the leaders who fight for us against Trump.
[**So, today, we’re asking you to make a donation to Mark Kelly’s campaign. If you can afford it — and only if you can afford it. With an important deadline tonight, there’s no better time.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-apr25.P7mRSa&refcode=em250430-1-500&t=1&akid=6057%2E6688874%2EFXKdHE)

Derek — In a minute, we’re going to ask if you can pitch in to support the DNC ahead of our end-of-month fundraising deadline. But first, we hope you’ll give us a chance to earn your first contribution of 2025: As Trump sends our economy into a tailspin and attacks our fundamental freedoms, it’s more important than ever that Democrats not only cut through the noise — but build the long-term infrastructure we’ll need to elect more leaders who can check Trump’s power in their states, cities, and districts. **That’s exactly what we’re doing.** So far this year, we’ve focused on organizing everywhere and investing in state parties. In fact, the DNC recently announced a _$1 million_ monthly investment in state parties across the country — an investment unlike anything Democrats have done in modern times. We’re already seeing the results when we show up everywhere: Since the year began, Democrats organized across Wisconsin and kept Elon Musk from buying a seat on the Supreme Court, overperformed in states like Florida, and even flipped a deep-red district in Pennsylvania. On top of that, we’re working to meet voters where they are, day in and day out. Democrats have shown up at more than 100 People’s Town Halls in communities nationwide — including in areas where Republican representatives are too scared to face their own constituents. And we’ve launched a new War Room operation, focused on driving aggressive daily messaging to counter the Trump administration, leveraging creative opposition tactics and an expansive research operation and combating lies from the far-right. **To fund all of this work, we’re counting on your support. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: I just reintroduced the Medicare For All Act in the House
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
I’ve said many times that we need to be more than an opposition party.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20250430-4999-footer&t=1&akid=4999%2E420207%2Egi3tgJ)
Peter,
I’ve said many times that we need to be more than an “opposition” party. We need to be a “proposition party” that fights for higher wages, lower costs, universal health care, and a government that actually works for the people.
**Yesterday, as part of that effort, I was proud to reintroduce the _Medicare For All Act_ in the House of Representatives.**
The current health care situation is cruel and completely unsustainable. Corporate greed has taken over the system, and at every turn, Americans are at risk of being pushed into severe medical debt.
Plus, billion-dollar pharmaceutical corporations are raising the prices of prescriptions and making it harder for everyday Americans to get the medicine they need.
It doesn’t have to be this way. Other nations have figured out how to deliver quality care without breaking the bank, and it’s time for us to join them.
**It’s time for Medicare For All, Peter.[If you agree, will you pitch in $3 to my campaign before midnight and help us reach our end-of-month goal? None of my work would be possible without your support.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20250430-1?refcode=em20250430-4999&amount=3&refcode2=4999_420207_gi3tgJ&akid=4999%2E420207%2Egi3tgJ)**

## The Kennedy Center Scraps a Week of Pride Month Events
For years, the Kennedy Center has promoted LGBT-related material, causes, and events. name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: I still have hope
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
#
Yesterday marked 100 days of the Trump administration. It’s worse than just about anything we could have feared. From the direct assault on our Constitution and the rule of law to his efforts to undermine every bulwark of our democracy, Trump is doing his best to destroy this country.
**But I still have hope.** Last Saturday, I held a town hall in Denton, Texas where more than 1,300 people came together to stand up and be counted for this country. We had a wonderful, open conversation about our future, what we’re each willing to do to make sure we come through and how we can organize to get it done.
When Trump tries to divide us, attack the vulnerable, and make us feel hopeless, we’ve got to join together, bring the outsiders in and give each other a reason to be hopeful.
I’m hoping to keep hitting the road and host more town halls so we can bring more people into Powered by People and the larger movement of saving our country.
[**If you can, will you chip in $5, $10, or $20 today to help ensure Powered by People has the resources to continue to host town halls in Texas?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20250430.vEsnkk&refcode=ema20250430-240093&t=1&akid=240093%2E444211%2Ehe0taK)
Thank you,
Beto

subject: 50 years ago today, Saigon fell
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Cedar Key Progress and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
| | | It’s Kenton, founder of Cedar Key Progress.
Fifty years ago today on April 30, 1975, Saigon fell.
My grandparents and parents, part of the ethnic Chinese minority in Vietnam, were stuck in Saigon as the last American helicopters left.
In the aftermath, whether they could obtain an exit permit or not, millions fled any way they could.
It took over a decade for both sides of my family to make it to freedom in the United States.
**Through their sacrifice and the ironclad law of the United States Constitution, I was born on our soil as a citizen, with democracy as my birthright.**
[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquatmgZTEMuLQ1bf-_rXJuO3YbgPpASNBD5VcYYax6A02r1hbaPRA-JLEy9shQrRfVvv9q2d_I4pVJhBJiQwZEKAJRoeMKVZMpTgn_PLtzZdTo2VC5BC3Q5ZL2_R9zwJk0pbD_2Y6q3K34ueNhz5IMBVqIDtjw_X8WnTG8xRmvEEYny5vYd7hAjk659HitM5LytQFnFf6ixoCPuepWswsLW0V0AYSH0JuCjPWkc_-63hSYaePLVZF_kTACbb3OIUnaMeghASWNhXnw8GTFNZWvkiKTXwOH0b-hZqlPPkc9H01PLgocvUFXUzE12i8iddUAnU96R_Pcte5kH5nCAMF7HosQd_Jjpsd2kyfbGdPZ_wwX2WtFiu1RuxNpLGfyBpyk/4g3/ZUFXEjv9S5GoX5pkjcfT2A/h0/h001.GE5Z7nUnA1cEKjIRTCeRf2CShjHm-VrBFwhQSOLwUfI)_I took an early interest in elections._
**Friend, I started Cedar Key Progress to organize thousands of supporters like you to fight back against the greatest threat to our American democracy and values: Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans.**
White nationalist Republicans attack family reunification, which allowed my parents to be united with their brothers and sisters, as "chain migration."
They denounce children of immigrants like me the "Great Replacement", and even want to end birthright citizenship.
They _really_ wish I hadn’t been born.
They're closing off refugee resettlement, detaining and hassling citizens for the crime of looking not white, and even deporting native-born US citizens without any process.
And they worship Donald Trump - a disgusting career criminal who wants to rule for life, a fascist who commits impeachable crimes and insults our Constitution with impunity.
Think back to how you became an American - whether you’re a Native American, an immigrant, or you’re descended from one.
In many parts of the world, it's not easy to be fully accepted if you aren't part of the nation's dominant ethnic group.
**But the United States of America was not founded on an ethnicity or a religion, it was founded on ideas: that all are created equal, that we are governed by the consent of the people, for life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.**
White nationalist MAGA Republicans don’t agree.
They have a narrow vision of who Americans ought to be that excludes minorities - racial, gender, sexual, religious, or more - anyone that doesn’t fit in their dreams.
They censor and condemn our diversity, instead of celebrating it.
**Fifty years ago today, the country my parents were born in ceased to exist.** **
** **Now, I fight to ensure the America I was born in stays a free and fair democracy for centuries to come.**
