clean_body: | | | It’s Kenton, founder of Cedar Key Progress. Fifty years ago today on April 30, 1975, Saigon fell. My grandparents and parents, part of the ethnic Chinese minority in Vietnam, were stuck in Saigon as the last American helicopters left. In the aftermath, whether they could obtain an exit permit or not, millions fled any way they could. It took over a decade for both sides of my family to make it to freedom in the United States. Through their sacrifice and the ironclad law of the United States Constitution, I was born on our soil as a citizen, with democracy as my birthright. took an early interest in elections. Friend, I started Cedar Key Progress to organize thousands of supporters like you to fight back against the greatest threat to our American democracy and values: Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans. White nationalist Republicans attack family reunification, which allowed my parents to be united with their brothers and sisters, as "chain migration." They denounce children of immigrants like me the "Great Replacement", and even want to end birthright citizenship. They really wish I hadn’t been born. They're closing off refugee resettlement, detaining and hassling citizens for the crime of looking not white, and even deporting native-born US citizens without any process. And they worship Donald Trump - a disgusting career criminal who wants to rule for life, a fascist who commits impeachable crimes and insults our Constitution with impunity. Think back to how you became an American - whether you’re a Native American, an immigrant, or you’re descended from one. In many parts of the world, it's not easy to be fully accepted if you aren't part of the nation's dominant ethnic group. But the United States of America was not founded on an ethnicity or a religion, it was founded on ideas: that all are created equal, that we are governed by the consent of the people, for life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. White nationalist MAGA Republicans don’t agree. They have a narrow vision of who Americans ought to be that excludes minorities - racial, gender, sexual, religious, or more - anyone that doesn’t fit in their dreams. They censor and condemn our diversity, instead of celebrating it. Fifty years ago today, the country my parents were born in ceased to exist. Now, I fight to ensure the America I was born in stays a free and fair democracy for centuries to come. Hi, it’s Oregon Secretary of State, Tobias Read.
One of the most essential elements of my job is overseeing Oregon’s elections and ensuring they are free and fair.
However, President Trump thinks running elections for all 50 states falls within his purview. Earlier this year, he issued an executive order trying to take control of state-level elections, making it harder for voters to cast their ballots, disenfranchising millions, and undermining the security of our elections.
It is antidemocratic and illegal, so Oregon and 20 other states filed lawsuits to stop his executive order. And thankfully, a judge issued an injunction.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250430em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250430em]
But this is not over. It’s an ongoing battle, and we must be ready for any disruptions in our election systems, whether natural disasters, human disasters, or policy disasters.
Trump’s actions infringe on the responsibility of states and localities to run their elections, and I will not stand for it. Trump does not have the authority to govern Oregon elections—that’s my job, as do the 36 dedicated county clerks around our state .
I hope you'll have my back. Please rush a donation of any amount to my team right now to power my work – I still need to raise another $3,450 before midnight tonight, and I’m counting on your help to get there. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250430em]

body:
In less than four months, Trump has destroyed jobs, brought the economy to the brink of ruin, and done absolutely nothing to lower prices for working people. | | | Peter, Calling Trump’s first 101 days a dumpster fire would be an insult to dumpster fires. In less than four months, Trump has destroyed jobs, brought the economy to the brink of ruin, and done absolutely nothing to lower prices for working people. But Trump’s failures are not the full story of these first 101 days. How we’ve _responded_ to his train wreck of a presidency is a big story too. Because no matter how Fox News and the White House press team try to spin it, **the people aren’t fooled.** They see what’s going on. It’s why millions took the streets this month to protest Trump and Musk’s attacks on working families. It’s why more and more people are joining community organizations or stepping up to run for office ([you can too!](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtZzzfTY2NadQ7R1AXSz5TeyTfM0ix-gIfhfpnO48n3XdEZeCYiAzG-MYOp_GUSggy2YQ2sZQOfXCaUUyrxe_sr6-zZJd5DtP3Rd0XeJwGJHH-JPcJCnUmd27HgJ0gwfBkAkCdMqgpeF44GZDuZapW8nLXNvXcwjClUmRcuCZrZF5Mb1Ql-KIe8p1Z94MpMvmP6hyMb9ZabOAld7SHtfDh9122RPowxImdRB02_85C5-aSc262EGQxnL11wA9LZqKeDVuWn6V6UWHd8vaJihVF2VMf9ILVo1qOL_GujaHuGIM/4g3/6wPXAio9T2GRLWZSx8Uq0g/h0/h001.fGSwC_fxQWmZqzVsiXBqiV3lult4xS2EKH59bvLhfxM)). And it’s why, in spite of Trump’s efforts to drive our nation toward fascism, **we are CONTINUING to bring working people together, from every background and geography, to stop him and his MAGA cronies in their tracks.** [**If you want to join us in this fight, consider making an end-of-month donation today. We rely on your support in order to build a new type of government, run by working families FOR working families.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9D5qDaq26IF8-OYFDKADUgmaceKY4iKpG3nKUXZJ66mYhmQenvz_wvhO8dw0pz8wF_wCEIJbM8MdnL8zHProYW7fhDXHtXSuhMGrbjc5FMhpMcOxCX3hsECzVJJsqOB3ndbi1ICgP-INE20cFOhTmT2xJooRT_7EddsS2C3tn5GATgK3pNn3lty-1phYRW8UwgCMQscbK8GFn3yz3N5dUkpTdvK7r70Tudz7PfPxt0mD9VwsigHBZSIFk4Z_S54KoXfcIOrLAM63Qhv8Jm0oXkLd-fyskYKqyC26zpWWztJZHHPT8MdVB1vgjf1Ku3p_QAj8LYIvcEOt1Eqia9oIYgSTC0B9fRl79-WBunIJGRso/4g3/6wPXAio9T2GRLWZSx8Uq0g/h1/h001.-FVHiuE1-uJcBoOkMzXRkjxBWfmG7pR4Rp1qVQ6Zuik) **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9D5qDaq26IF8-OYFDKADUgmaceKY4iKpG3nKUXZJ66mZQksRxDTD9FyZzQ8m6F8isvMAeOFmmepq0eGRjc4tRs2sfGQoJDcjXRSbZJlzf1tapw1TBf_qor4pOYb129MrdNEkSQ_joNKGgu1hdx4GiQ9vWWR6KU6mWavgC-Yq2WM-8p5roXrtPOHfbbScwuGWxmlzKQwfBByhbfs5i4hidfLe5I3Rqyw4eL6DE8zjtoBnuv1MmgveLKylFi0bYRQayfe9K_S95WNk8mB_6lRAS7VRUnMlRToVE_qsUa0EXeP9fo7Bk8e8J-aN3toJ0eecqgq8CI7JEu8n0N4KOT1Mb2XMI7mDCVKXC1CRfYRAWmuM/4g3/6wPXAio9T2GRLWZSx8Uq0g/h2/h001.zO5av662aaueK3MGB3d8hG2NSV-Cur7UOq-jd4sMdAs)** Here’s just a few of the things we’ve been up to these past 101 days: **Nationwide** , thousands of you have already signed up to learn more about being a WFP candidate in virtually every state. Tens of thousands of you have been attending town halls (in Republican districts) to make your voices heard. And millions of you have shown up in the streets at one of the hundreds of _Hands Off!_ protests around the country. In **Wisconsin** , we showed up to take on Elon Musk and turn out the vote for Judge Susan Crawford, helping her defeat the extreme candidate Musk spent $25 million trying to elect. In **Maryland** , progressives now hold a majority in Prince George’s County after WFP candidates Aisha Braveboy and Shayla Adams-Stafford won special elections. In **Rhode Island** , WFP lawmakers introduced bills to stop an energy company’s monopoly and bar them from using consumer revenue to lobby for higher rates and to buy private planes and spa visits for executives.1 In **Washington** , voters in Seattle approved a WFP-endorsed ballot initiative to fund social housing, and taxing wealthy businesses.2 In **Pennsylvania** , WFP champions on Philadelphia’s city council are fighting tooth and nail to pass the People’s Tax Plan,3 as well as saving the city’s current policy around free public transit. In **Connecticut** , our members are working hard on tax reforms of their own, which would divert some of that revenue out of the pockets of the wealthy and back into city budgets and services.4 In **Colorado** , we successfully beat back an attempt to cut wages for tipped workers.5 And have been fighting in the state legislature to protect immigrants,6 enshrine voting rights, strengthen labor rights, and safeguard access to reproductive and gender-affirming care.7 And we haven’t even touched on all the incredible work that’s being done, day in and day out, by WFP chapters and allies around the country. The point is, we cannot and WILL not just roll over and let Trump’s authoritarian ambitions win. And our _opposition_ to him will not magically result in victory overnight, either. It’s a long road. And we are proud to walk shoulder to shoulder with each and every one of you on it. clean_body: In less than four months, Trump has destroyed jobs, brought the economy to the brink of ruin, and done absolutely nothing to lower prices for working people. | | | Peter, Calling Trump’s first 101 days a dumpster fire would be an insult to dumpster fires. In less than four months, Trump has destroyed jobs, brought the economy to the brink of ruin, and done absolutely nothing to lower prices for working people. But Trump’s failures are not the full story of these first 101 days. How we’ve responded to his train wreck of a presidency is a big story too. Because no matter how Fox News and the White House press team try to spin it, the people aren’t fooled. They see what’s going on. It’s why millions took the streets this month to protest Trump and Musk’s attacks on working families. It’s why more and more people are joining community organizations or stepping up to run for office (). And it’s why, in spite of Trump’s efforts to drive our nation toward fascism, we are CONTINUING to bring working people together, from every background and geography, to stop him and his MAGA cronies in their tracks. Here’s just a few of the things we’ve been up to these past 101 days: Nationwide , thousands of you have already signed up to learn more about being a WFP candidate in virtually every state. Tens of thousands of you have been attending town halls (in Republican districts) to make your voices heard. And millions of you have shown up in the streets at one of the hundreds of Hands Off! protests around the country. In Wisconsin , we showed up to take on Elon Musk and turn out the vote for Judge Susan Crawford, helping her defeat the extreme candidate Musk spent $25 million trying to elect. In Maryland , progressives now hold a majority in Prince George’s County after WFP candidates Aisha Braveboy and Shayla Adams-Stafford won special elections. In Rhode Island , WFP lawmakers introduced bills to stop an energy company’s monopoly and bar them from using consumer revenue to lobby for higher rates and to buy private planes and spa visits for executives.1 In Washington , voters in Seattle approved a WFP-endorsed ballot initiative to fund social housing, and taxing wealthy businesses.2 In Pennsylvania , WFP champions on Philadelphia’s city council are fighting tooth and nail to pass the People’s Tax Plan,3 as well as saving the city’s current policy around free public transit. In Connecticut , our members are working hard on tax reforms of their own, which would divert some of that revenue out of the pockets of the wealthy and back into city budgets and services.4 In Colorado , we successfully beat back an attempt to cut wages for tipped workers.5 And have been fighting in the state legislature to protect immigrants,6 enshrine voting rights, strengthen labor rights, and safeguard access to reproductive and gender-affirming care.7 And we haven’t even touched on all the incredible work that’s being done, day in and day out, by WFP chapters and allies around the country. The point is, we cannot and WILL not just roll over and let Trump’s authoritarian ambitions win. And our opposition to him will not magically result in victory overnight, either. It’s a long road. And we are proud to walk shoulder to shoulder with each and every one of you on it. When I was first sworn into office in the New Jersey General Assembly and State Senate, I made a promise to fight for the families of New Jersey--and I have been delivering on that promise ever since.

And now in Congress since 2023, I have continued to put the families of New Jersey at the forefront of my work in the nation's capital and made progress on the issues that matter most to our communities.

I have built a strong track record of delivering results and fighting to:

🇺🇸 **Secure our Borders** **🇺🇸 Lower the cost of living** **🇺🇸 Ensure the safety of our communities** **🇺🇸 Bring real solutions to New Jersey families

** But our work is not done--****_not by a long shot.

This race is set to be one of the most competitive in the country next year, and I’m determined to flip it from red to blue. But to do it, I need your help. [Will you join my campaign and Blue Amp Action as a Founding Donor?](https://default.salsalabs.org/T44a1a087-bc53-488b-a442-4c4f05f8af01/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

| I’m a pastor’s son who grew up learning how to stretch a dollar in Corona, California. I turned a love of music into a career and got lucky, making it big as a member of the award-winning band OneRepublic. But it wasn’t always easy. I got signed, got dropped, and had to start over. Through all that, I saw how the industry took advantage of people—just like we’re seeing now in Washington. The people in charge are screwing people over just to make a buck. Trump, Musk, and these clowns in Washington are cutting cancer research, veterans’ health care, and funding for our schools. They’re getting into trade wars with Canada and Mexico, making everything we buy more expensive. And all the while, they’re using what they take from us to give billionaires another tax cut they don’t need. The status quo isn’t working. It’s how we ended up here. We need leaders who will stand up and say enough is enough. I’m not running for Congress to be a politician or to build wealth or power like some others do. I’m running because I’m a father who wants a better future for my children and for all of our children. Right now, our current representation is more focused on giving tax cuts to wealthy donors and elite circles in Washington, DC, than addressing the real issues we face here at home. I’m running to address the affordability crisis, help small businesses, address the climate crisis, prevent gun violence, and so much more. But I can’t do it alone; I need your help. Over the past decade it has infected democratic societies--including ours. It is as simple as it is terrifying: What we do now will define the future of our country and world. We at Blue Amp Action are dedicated to liberal, open societies, where reason and science are applied to solve our problems; where civil rights--including voting rights!--are protected for all. We fight for these values every day. Speaking up on our platforms, raising the voices and the political prospects of liberal pols and pundits. **And savvy grassroots activists like you know, just like we do, that we can’t stop watching the people we help elect:_ after the elections, we have to keep organizing support for the policies we like and pushing back against the ones we don’t._** **__When the public tunes out between elections and the only people our elected officials hear from are the paid lobbyists of wealthy corporations, our government stops being accountable to the needs of ordinary families.__** **Democracy never sleeps, and neither can we.** So we ask that you support our work, so we can continue to engage in this fight every moment of every day. ### Cliff's Edge: Trump Lies, Moran Blinks & Democracy Dies a Little More Inside
If you want a masterclass in how a democracy limps toward fascism in $5,000 shoes and a red tie long enough to hang below Donald Trump's d*k, look no further than Trump's latest "interview" with ABC's Terry Moran. Trump lies like humans breathe and MAGAs snort Kool-Aid. Yet, there was Moran, **the physical embodiment of a human shrug** , meekly accepting it like he was about to say "Vladimir, Stawp.. ."
_Trump unleashed his usual allotment of verbal sewage:_ He claimed MS-13 is pouring across the border unchecked (lie), Biden wants open borders (lie) and Moran should be _grateful_ --**grateful!** --for the privilege of interviewing America's very own half-sentient goulash of meat-puppet & expired spray tan. Instead of fighting back, Moran seemed more concerned that he not scuff the emperor's gold-plated jackboots.
This is how it happens. **You put a game show host with a Pol Pot temperament and OJ 's ethics behind the Resolute Desk**, and pair him with a journalist who seemed to livestream down his leg because the mean man might yell at him again. And Trump doesn't just lie--he seeks to dominate these interactions, as winning and losing is all there is to this sad-sack of human bankruptcy. He snarls, scolds, expands like the Dilophosaurus that whacks _Newman_ in _Jurassic Park_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cdc4a136-6e09-4daf-a812-73033e4280eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Trump turns every setting into a mob trial, while most of the press corps still acts like they're covering Eisenhower's golf swing. The media, especially those chained to corporate giants more interested in _access_ than _accountability_ , have internalized the idea that fact-checking in real time's rude, challenging a demagogue is "bias." This isn't journalism--it's masturbatory hagiography with a multi-watt broadcast signal.
_This is a moment where I take a quick break to say there are still good reporters in corporate media. Those who don 't buckle to an Orban-esque Ork. But they dwindle by the day._
Ok, we continue. There were lies--MANY--but let's just analyze the the capo di tutti capi of Trump's deceit. Trump looked Moran in the face and said an innocent man, Kilmar Abrego Garcia--currently locked in a concentration camp in El Salvador--was a member of MS-13 because _Garcia has MS-13 tattooed on his knuckles_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e68a703d-7155-435b-b74e-7f58fe3342c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

**This was a moment that defines our era** , and not just because of Trump's willingness to toss out a conspiracy equal in stupid-person believability to:...

body:
Make your voice heard today!
|

Peter,
Extremists in Congress are pushing an extreme anti-voter bill — the SAVE Act — that would make it harder, if not impossible, for millions of voters across the country to register to vote. **We need your help to stop it.**
The SAVE Act would force every voter to provide a passport or birth certificate every time they register or update their voter registration which would effectively end online and mail-in voter registration.
About half of American citizens **— _ nearly 150 million citizens _— **do not have a passport, and elderly Americans are one of the demographics least likely to have a passport. This would also disproportionately impact military voters, tribal communities, rural Americans, disaster survivors, people of color, and working-class Americans — silencing eligible voters and undermining our democracy.
This bill isn’t about election integrity. It’s about silencing voters. There’s _zero evidence of widespread voter fraud,_ and states already have secure systems in place to verify voter eligibility. **The real goal of the SAVE Act? To make it harder for eligible Americans to vote.**

Sen. Markwayne Mullin **[sparred with CNN's Kaitlan Collins](https://substack.com/redirect/6eb93f6e-9f07-4421-8cc0-aa90b9cbfba1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for claiming that President Trump is "wildly exaggerating" the reduction in consumer costs during his first 100 days.
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/6eb93f6e-9f07-4421-8cc0-aa90b9cbfba1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6eb93f6e-9f07-4421-8cc0-aa90b9cbfba1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Collins challenged Trump's claim that the cost of eggs were down 87%, "if they were, people would be paying $.50 for a dozen eggs which obviously you know that they're not."
"Well the fact is they're down!" Mullin fired back. "At the height they were at 9.1%, so it depends what metric you're using,... they're down to 2.4% now inflation, that's a significant drop!"
"Why not just say they're down 52% or 53% instead of 87%?" Collins pushed back.
Mullins called out Collins and CNN for not caring this much about consumer inflation during the Biden administration as it was soaring to unspeakable heights. "Why was it in the first 100 days the President was able to bring down inflation to 2.4% and have $5 trillion of investments into the United States?! Why wasn't that happening during the last 4 years of the Biden administration?!!"
Collins disagreed that the Biden administration wasn't held to account by the media for their disastrous economy, before steering the conversation to Trump's recent polling.
"Is there any sense when you look at those numbers that the White House needs to change course?" Collins asked the Senator.
Mullin again emphasized the $5 trillion the Trump administration secured in economic investment in the U.S. as well as a steep drop in inflation. "Numbers don't lie!"

# Robert DeNiro's son comes out as transgender
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8bc69bed-e739-4b54-a8c8-1e6b874c9a5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Airyn De Niro, formerly Aaron, the 29-year-old child of actor Robert De Niro, has publicly come out as a transgender woman during an interview with LGBTQ focused outlet "Them."
"There's a difference between being visible and being seen," Airyn told the outlet. "I've been visible. I don't think I've been seen yet."
De Niro, a longtime Trump hater, has 7 children with 4 different women. Airyn's mother is actress Toukie Smith, who dated De Niro from 1988 to 1996.
"I wasn't brought up having a side part in one of dad's movies or going to business meetings or attending premieres. My dad was very big on us finding our own sort of path... I would want [success] to happen on my own merit," Airyn explained.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e6ed68d6-57b4-4eb4-a299-950a7862767e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
voiceofairyn/Instagram
"Obviously, no parent is perfect, but I am grateful that both my parents agreed to keep me out of the limelight," he continued. "They have told me they wanted me to have as much of a normal childhood as possible."
Airyn said he hoped to be an inspiration for "at least one other person like me who is black, who is queer, who's not a size extra small."

# GOP Senator fact checks CNN on the spot during disappointing live interview
U.S. Secretary of the interior Doug Burgum **[ran circles around CNN's Kaitlan Collins](https://substack.com/redirect/723eaa9d-c5a5-46eb-be51-b2c1d8afc34f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with facts on Trump's tariffs her liberal logic could not rebuke.
[Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/723eaa9d-c5a5-46eb-be51-b2c1d8afc34f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/723eaa9d-c5a5-46eb-be51-b2c1d8afc34f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In the segment, Collins pressed Burgum on the effectiveness of Trump's international tariffs to promote American domestic production.
"What do you say to the small business owners who look at that and say, you know, the big companies are getting a break but we, because we're small businesses, are not?" Collins asked.
"**[If a small retailer is buying goods and selling goods that is made in the United States, tariffs aren't a part of their life.](https://substack.com/redirect/723eaa9d-c5a5-46eb-be51-b2c1d8afc34f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** There are no tariffs on products made in the United States."
The conversation transitioned to energy, and the current administration's efforts to make it affordable for Americans.
"Every sector depends on energy. President Trump has wisely kept energy out of all these tariff discussions."
"**[Any country that does not have their own energy security, has no national security](https://substack.com/redirect/723eaa9d-c5a5-46eb-be51-b2c1d8afc34f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** ," Burgum said.
Collins then made a fatal error, crediting the Biden administration for the highest levels of American oil production.
Burgum immediately steered her straight.
"**[All time oil production under Biden was because of Trump! It was in spite of Biden.](https://substack.com/redirect/723eaa9d-c5a5-46eb-be51-b2c1d8afc34f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I was running a state that was a natural resources states, and we were fighting the Federal Government. The Federal Government wasn't even holding the legally required lease sales during the Biden Administration," Burgum said.
"They didn't take responsibility because it wasn't very popular with their voters," Collins meagerly countered.
"Affordable electricity is popular with everyone, and America needs to make sure we don't lose the thing. I mean, take a look at what's happening in Europe right now with this 60 million people in a blackout, brownout. We came very close to that happening in America because the Biden Administration policy so dangerously eroded baseload in favor of having unreliable, intermittent sources," Burgum said.
Watch Burgum brutally fact check Collins on live T.V.:

Peter — I know we ask a lot of you. And I know you’ve got a lot on your plate.

But here’s the thing: this movement is about you, for you, and it only works if I have you standing with me.

Growing up, I never even dreamed I’d get into politics. I was raised by a single mom in a mobile home park. I watched my mom work hard and complete her teaching degree over nine years while raising us kids.
We lived just a few doors down from my grandmother, who worked into her 70s. I’ll never forget her advice:
**“No matter what work you do, always do more than what they ask of you.”**
I looked to those words as my guide as I worked my way through college and to help lead a major Minnesota manufacturing company.
And I’ve kept that advice in mind during my six plus years in the House representing Minnesota’s 2nd District — successfully capping the cost of insulin at $35 a month for seniors on Medicare.

name: Bobby Jindal
subject: Fox News Op-Ed: The American people will support Medicaid reform. Here's why
body:
A majority of Americans believe able-bodied adults on Medicaid should have to work to receive the program’s benefits| | |
---
| | **The American people will support Medicaid reform. Here's why** _A majority of Americans believe able-bodied adults on Medicaid should have to work to receive the program’s benefits_ By Bobby Jindal and Newt Gingrich Democrats and the left-wing media are presently demonizing Republicans for wanting to make Medicaid more accountable and affordable.

They are counting on the program’s general popularity to inoculate it from any real change. However, a recent survey by America’s New Majority Project found most Americans support commonsense reforms to modernize and improve Medicaid – including those who use it.

For example, a majority of Americans believe able-bodied adults on Medicaid should have to work to receive the program’s benefits. The survey found 78% of Americans support work requirements for Medicaid and other safety net programs. This includes 89% of Republicans, 75% of independents, and 70% of Democrats. It also includes 66% of Americans on Medicaid and 70% of Americans who have received welfare benefits in the past year. This fits the pattern we saw in 1996. subject: A humble request before our deadline at midnight
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
You know what’s happening, but most people still don’t. If we’re going to build a movement that stops and reverses Trump’s power grab, we have to start reaching the people who aren’t reading the news every day.
#

Peter, we’ve got just a few hours until our end of month deadline at midnight tonight.
That deadline comes at a moment unlike any other in our nation’s history.
I served in Iraq as a Marine at the height of the war, about 20 years ago. All those years ago, I never thought I’d see the President of the United States sign off on the arrest of a sitting judge on virtually nonexistent charges. I never thought I’d see the President of the United States blatantly ignore the Supreme Court. I signed up to serve to defend our Constitution — to make sure exactly that kind of thing never happened at home.
This is authoritarianism. It is here. And we need to stand up now or risk losing the rights and liberties we were born with.
You know what’s happening, but most people still don’t. If we’re going to build a movement that stops and reverses Trump’s power grab, we have to start reaching the people who aren’t reading the news every day.
That’s why I’m getting on cable news all the time. It’s why I’m doing podcasts and social media, interviews with local and national papers. It’s why I’m doing town halls all over Arizona, and why I hope to do more soon.
That’s what I did in my campaign. It’s what I’ve been doing since I got elected. And I’m going to keep doing it as long as I have to until we start to break through to people.

Many of my Republican colleagues are probably on the phones right now begging for large checks to fund their campaigns to hold onto the House next year.

In return, they are beholden to the interests of their mega-donors at the expense of everyday Americans. It’s called “Call Time,” _and it’s something I refuse to do._

subject: Raise your voice to help defend the Endangered Species Act
body:
Comment by May 19th!| | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106845712/542797079/779512579?sourceid=1167576&utm_campaign=action-alert&utm_medium=email&utm_source=aa-esa&Series=1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImU5MWE5ZTE0LTBkMjYtZjAxMS04YjNkLTYwNDViZGVkOGNjYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=JZI4LfhoZbKVoyNIx3hbPsirygFQGsxMW1pZypEazoE=&emci=2205cca4-7421-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=e91a9e14-0d26-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=1504551)

---
| | Dear Peter,

This is a critical moment for the animals and plants of the redwood forest.

The Department of Interior has proposed a change to the Endangered Species Act (ESA) that would gut protections for threatened wildlife and deal a harsh blow to redwood conservation.

Since 1973, the ESA has stood as one of America's most successful conservation laws, preventing the extinction of 99% of the species under its protection—from California condors to gray wolves to humpback whales. Now federal officials have proposed altering the ESA’s long-understood definition of the word “harm” to **_no longer include habitat destruction_. **

The recognition that habitat loss can harm a species just as much as direct injury is a crucial component of the ESA’s success. Unraveling this key protection strikes at the heart of wildlife conservation and the mission of Save the Redwoods League.

But you can help us oppose this dangerous change.

The newly proposed rule, called “Rescinding the Definition of ‘Harm’ Under the Endangered Species Act,” is subject to a public comment period through May 19, 2025. We urge you to speak up in defense of the ESA now and **[submit your public comment](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106845713/542797080/1155893031?sourceid=1167576&utm_campaign=action-alert&utm_medium=email&utm_source=aa-esa&Series=1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImU5MWE5ZTE0LTBkMjYtZjAxMS04YjNkLTYwNDViZGVkOGNjYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=JZI4LfhoZbKVoyNIx3hbPsirygFQGsxMW1pZypEazoE=&emci=2205cca4-7421-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=e91a9e14-0d26-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&ceid=1504551)**.
---
| |
---
| | In California’s redwood forests, removing habitat protections would have grave consequences. While the trees themselves are not listed under the ESA, redwood ecosystems are lifelines for a range of federally protected species. Cool, shaded streams sustain imperiled coho salmon and steelhead. Towering canopies shelter the endangered marbled murrelet and northern spotted owl. Damp forest floors host rare amphibians and plants found nowhere else on Earth. Rescinding the definition of harm **_opens these redwood ecosystems to threats_ **from mining, drilling, and industrial timber extraction. Without healthy and intact forests and waterways, the endangered species that depend on redwood forests simply will not survive. Threatened animals and plants need strong protection now more than ever. Join us in defending the Endangered Species Act—submit your public comment by the May 19 deadline.
---

clean_body: Comment by May 19th!| | | | | Dear Peter, This is a critical moment for the animals and plants of the redwood forest. The Department of Interior has proposed a change to the Endangered Species Act (ESA) that would gut protections for threatened wildlife and deal a harsh blow to redwood conservation. Since 1973, the ESA has stood as one of America's most successful conservation laws, preventing the extinction of 99% of the species under its protection—from California condors to gray wolves to humpback whales. Now federal officials have proposed altering the ESA’s long-understood definition of the word “harm” to no longer include habitat destruction. The recognition that habitat loss can harm a species just as much as direct injury is a crucial component of the ESA’s success. Unraveling this key protection strikes at the heart of wildlife conservation and the mission of Save the Redwoods League. But you can help us oppose this dangerous change. The newly proposed rule, called “Rescinding the Definition of ‘Harm’ Under the Endangered Species Act,” is subject to a public comment period through May 19, 2025. We urge you to speak up in defense of the ESA now and . | | | | In California’s redwood forests, removing habitat protections would have grave consequences. While the trees themselves are not listed under the ESA, redwood ecosystems are lifelines for a range of federally protected species. Cool, shaded streams sustain imperiled coho salmon and steelhead. Towering canopies shelter the endangered marbled murrelet and northern spotted owl. Damp forest floors host rare amphibians and plants found nowhere else on Earth. Rescinding the definition of harm opens these redwood ecosystems to threats from mining, drilling, and industrial timber extraction. Without healthy and intact forests and waterways, the endangered species that depend on redwood forests simply will not survive. Threatened animals and plants need strong protection now more than ever. Join us in defending the Endangered Species Act—submit your public comment by the May 19 deadline. Thank you, Save the Redwoods League | Top photo: The threatened Pacific fisher can’t survive without its home in mixed conifer forests throughout the Sierra Nevada range. Photo: Bethany Weeks/USFWS. Dear Fellow American,

I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future.

A movement is growing, led by progressives—but supported by many well-meaning Americans—to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

And after you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since 1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty." Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans.

The support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Larry P. Arnn

President Trump was in Michigan to celebrate his first 100 days in office, speaking to a fired up crowd about how finally we have a president that is a champion for workers, defending our borders and choosing Detroit over Beijing. What should be a continued celebration of the administration's accomplishments is marred by legacy media's coverage of the president. The Media Research Center revealed that 92% of the media's coverage of President Trump is negative. Amazon got a taste of FAFO, just as they intended to add a tariff upcharge on their website, their stock plummeted. Choosing China over the U.S. is a bad look and after serious backlash they walked back the tariff upcharge. Tammy Bruce is the Spokesperson for the U.S. State Department. On today's show she explains exactly how and why President Trump is approaching China. He is putting America back in the driver's seat so China can no longer proliferate their unfair trading practices on the U.S. and the rest of the world. Tammy updates us on where negotiations stand for peace in Ukraine. After his meeting with President Trump, Zelensky is on board, while Putin seems to be boxing himself in. Secretary Scott Turner of the U.S. Housing and Urban Development is fixing the housing crisis in America. By striping away burdensome regulations, HUD is actively addressing our homeless crisis and getting people the shelter they need. He is also eradicating the harm done by DEI and replacing them with "biologically sound" policies to keep women safe from biological men in shelters. David Horowitz passed last night, he was a leader in the Conservative movement and today we honor and remember his impact and legacy.

Today a federal judge ordered the Trump regime to release Palestinian American activist Mohsen Mahdawi from ICE prison. Mahdawi was arrested during his citizenship interiew for his "crime" of speaking of speaking up for Palestinian and Jewish humanity, in calling for an end to the genocide in Gaza.
Upon walking out of the ICE prison, Mahdawi declared, "I am not afraid of you Donald Trump!"--a direct message of courage and defiance to the President and aspiring autocrat. This moment signifies a step toward justice, and serves as a reminder of all those still suffering behind bars. **Let 's Address This.**
**Earnest Ask! I am doing everything in my power to stave off fascism in the United States, and I need your support. Subscribe and join more than 130,000+ fellow activists.**

## The Moment of Release From ICE Prison
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6340a6b0-285a-406a-add7-dca62bea3a5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In his order to release Mohsen Mahdawi, Federal U.S. District Judge Geoffrey W. Crawford said Mahdawi's release was "in the public interest," adding that continued ICE detention would have a "chilling effect" on protected free speech. He also added that the Trump regime had provided zero evidence that Mahdawi was of any form of danger to the United States or to the American people.
This flies in direct contrast to the claim from Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Mahdawi's arrest was necessary to stop speech that harmed U.S. foreign policy and support of Israel. Moreover, this ruling serves as important precedent for additional immigrants and legal residents held in ICE prison for their 'crime' of speaking up for justice and human rights for Palestinians. While Mahdawi's release is a welcomed step towards justice, it is a reminder of the work that remains before us.
**If you 're finding value in this content, please join our movement and subscribe.**

## The Work Before Us
The below image is a non-comprehensive list of Black and brown immigrants detained by ICE for the "crime" of speaking up for justice for Palestine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dce7b809-ac59-40e8-8f7c-08f0b83d1e0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The exact "logic" used to detain Mohsen Mahwadi is being used to detain each of the aforementioned individuals. This precedent is devastating for numerous reasons.
* First, because it undermines the basic civil rights of these persons.
* Second, it sets the precedent that the Trump regime can go after anyone it doesn't like.
* And third, because we know what comes next--concentration camps and death camps, both of which have also already begun. The Trump regime is building a 30,000 person facility concentration camp at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba for migrants, and is already sending innocent people to an El Salvador death camp. And to be sure, we should not be sending guilty people to death camps, either.

Sadly, corporate media remains asleep at the wheel, refusing to loudly sound the alarm on this fascism for what it is. But this is also nothing new.
For example, a March 28, 1933 Seattle Times editorial concluded, "_There is no organized mistreatment of Jews in Germany_." Meanwhile, the Jews were on the verge of mass genocide. The Trump MAGA regime has already made clear their desire to repeat the injustices of Hitler's Nazi regime. The parallels are not hyperbolic, but mirror images. Consider Trump's strategy to deny due process, ignore the need for warrants, and simply raid the homes of people with impunity.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f7c8ccde-8c9a-4a8d-afe3-9199475c3b02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As the Holocaust Encyclopedia reminds us, this is precisely what Hitler's Nazi regime enacted as a matter of sustained national policy leading up to the Holocaust.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/669a766f-78f4-4d93-b007-7cf79f237ede?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And let's also talk about who the Trump regime is _not_ targeting.
There are over 500,000 undocumented white immigrants in the United States. Canadians. Europeans. Some of them overstayed visas, some arrived without documentation at all. But when was the last time you saw ICE raiding their homes, schools, places of worship, or hospitals? You don't see Ron DeSantis holding them in jail. You don't see Greg Abbott attacking them in his speeches. You don't see Trump scapegoating them at his rallies.
Why? Because they have what Trump and his ilk prize most: the complexion for protection. This is a stark reminder of the need for solidarity of all people in this country against these injustices.
Sadly, our lawmakers refused to act when they had the chance. We all recall how law enforcement engaged in no knock raids against Black Americans and killed innocent people like Breonna Taylor in Kentucky and Amir Locke in Minnesota. In fact, in the last decade alone American police [have killed ](https://substack.com/redirect/af743655-b5e0-4a9d-ba8f-38bba3431076?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[dozens](https://substack.com/redirect/af743655-b5e0-4a9d-ba8f-38bba3431076?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[of Americans while conducting no knock, often warrantless raids](https://substack.com/redirect/af743655-b5e0-4a9d-ba8f-38bba3431076?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against American citizens under the guise of combatting drug proliferation. And yet, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act failed to pass the Senate in two consecutive sessions because Republicans opposed it and corporate 'Democrats' Manchin and Sinema refused to abolish the Jim Crow filibuster to pass it. Is it any surprise that the Trump regime is escalating that policy against all people for any reason?

## Conclusion
What happened to Mohsen Mahdawi is not an aberration--it is a warning. It is a warning that the Trump regime is not flirting with fascism, it is enforcing it. It is not gesturing toward authoritarianism, it is codifying it. Mahdawi's release is a hard-fought victory, but it does not undo the injustice he endured, nor does it release the many others still behind bars for daring to speak out for justice. If the government can arrest someone during a citizenship interview for calling for peace, then no one who dares speak truth to power is safe.
That's why we must stay vigilant. We must keep organizing, raising our voices, and protecting one another. Because this isn't just about immigrants. This is about the future of American democracy itself. And while corporate media remains complicit in its silence, we will not be silent. We will expose these injustices, demand accountability, and fight like hell to ensure that this country lives up to its promise of liberty and justice for all--not just for the white, wealthy, and well-connected.
Let Mohsen's courage be our call to action. Be not afraid. And frankly, speak even if your voice shakes. Let's not wait for the next name or the next raid to finally act. Let's act now. Let's build a nation where no one is imprisoned for their beliefs, where no child fears a knock at the door, and where justice does not come as an exception--but as the rule.
**Before you go. I am doing everything in my power to stave off fascism under this new administration. I cannot do it alone. Subscribe below and join the movement.**

name: FRC Action
subject: Here's how you can stand up for peaceful pro-life protesters
body:
Please read the following message from our sponsor.
* * *

| | | | [](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63)
---
|
---
Dear Friend, The Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances (FACE) Act allows the U.S. government to prosecute anyone who blocks access to facilities that provide reproductive health services. Since this law defines "reproductive health services" as including services related to "the termination of a pregnancy," this protection applies to not only hospitals, doctor's offices, and pro-life pregnancy resource centers but also abortion facilities. **However, the evidence shows that the FACE Act has been enforced in a politically biased manner, most notably by the Biden administration!** Since the law was enacted in 1994, there have been over 200 prosecutions against pro-life individuals. (Several of them were elderly grandmothers who were peacefully praying at the time of their arrests!) In contrast, only six pro-abortion individuals have been prosecuted, despite the numerous cases of violence against pro-life pregnancy resource centers since the U.S. Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_! **This means approximately 97 percent of FACE Act prosecutions have been against pro-life Americans. This is not just.**
---
[](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63) **[Sign the Petiton Now](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63)** [](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63)
---
What's more, the Biden administration accounted for approximately one-quarter of all FACE Act prosecutions in the law's 30-year history! On January 23, 2025, President Trump pardoned 23 peaceful pro-life protestors prosecuted under the Biden administration, fulfilling a pledge he had made as a presidential candidate in 2023 at FRC Action's Pray Vote Stand Summit. We are grateful for this action by President Trump. Now, Congress must do its part! **[Please sign this petition below calling for Congress to take action against misuse of government power and repeal the FACE Act!](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63)**
---
[](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63) **[Help Repeal The FACE Act](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63)** [](https://click.em.dcdailyjournal.com/t/c/4e656e41270e4d209ec35a1a7d4413a0-26b6109863414c5a9f73fa0e92ba0ce8/63)
---
|
---
To Congressional leadership, The Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances (FACE) Act allows the U.S. government to prosecute anyone who blocks access to facilities that provide reproductive health services.1 Since this law defines "reproductive health services" as including services related to "the termination of a pregnancy,"2 this protection applies to not only hospitals, doctor's offices, and pro-life pregnancy resource centers but also abortion facilities. However, the enforcement of this law has been overwhelmingly one-sided. According to data acquired from the U.S. Department of Justice by the office of Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas), there have been over 200 FACE Act prosecutions against pro-life individuals since the law's enactment in 1994. Several of them were elderly grandmothers who were peacefully praying at the time of their arrests. In contrast, there have only been six prosecutions against pro-abortion individuals, despite the numerous cases of violence against pro-life pregnancy resource centers since the U.S. Supreme Court's decision to overturn _Roe v. Wade_ (_Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization_ , 2022). This means approximately **97 percent of FACE Act prosecutions have been against pro-life Americans**.3 Furthermore, at least 55 of the FACE Act prosecution cases were during the first three years of the Biden administration. In other words, three years of the Biden administration accounted for approximately one-quarter of all prosecutions in the FACE Act's 30-year history.4 The evidence indicates that the FACE Act has been enforced in a politically biased manner. Catholic speaker Mark Houck often prayed outside of an abortion facility in Philadelphia. On one occasion, a Planned Parenthood employee began shouting profanities and vulgar comments at Mark and his 12-year-old son. When Mark asked the employee to back off from his son, the employee refused, and Mark shoved him. A year later, in 2022, Mark was arrested for allegedly violating the FACE Act during this incident. FBI agents raided his home and handcuffed him in front of his wife and children.5 It's no stretch to conclude that the Biden-era U.S. Department of Justice's prosecution of this minor incident was meant to intimidate Mark and other pro-life Americans. On January 23, 2025, President Trump pardoned 23 peaceful pro-life protestors prosecuted under the Biden administration, fulfilling a pledge he had made as a presidential candidate in 2023 at FRC Action's Pray Vote Stand Summit. We are grateful for this action by President Trump and trust that his administration will not use the FACE Act improperly. However, there is always the possibility that this law could be misused by future administrations. Therefore, it is essential that Congress repeal the FACE Act so that pro-life Americans are not subjected to the same one-sided enforcement witnessed during the Biden years. We call upon members of Congress to support Rep. Chip Roy's bill to repeal the FACE Act. **Pro-life Americans deserve fair and equal treatment under the law, and their First Amendment right to pray outside abortion facilities should be protected.** We ask Congress to take action against misuse of government power by repealing the FACE Act.
---
|
---
P.S. FRC Action is the legislative affiliate of Family Research Council. FRC Action exists to be your Christian voice in Washington, D.C. as we educate and influence elected officials, engage our grassroots network, and mobilize voters on behalf of faith, family, and freedom.
---

2 18 USC § 248(e)(5).
3 Eireann Van Natta, "EXCLUSIVE: DOJ Data Confirms Conservative Fears Biden Weaponized Justice System," _The Daily Caller_ , July 30, 2024,

5 Dan Hart, "FBI Sends Team of Agents to Arrest Pro-Lifer While Making No Arrests for PRC, Church Attacks," _The Washington Stand_ , September 26, 2022,

Social Security is a lifeline for over 70 million Americans.

So far, Donald Trump and Elon Musk have attempted to close Social Security offices, lay off staff and more.

Now, many Americans can’t even get in touch with a Social Security representative to discuss their benefits. clean_body: Social Security is a lifeline for over 70 million Americans. So far, Donald Trump and Elon Musk have attempted to close Social Security offices, lay off staff and more. Now, many Americans can’t even get in touch with a Social Security representative to discuss their benefits. According to recent reports, the rate of “agent busy” messages shot up from 1.5% in February to 28.4% in March. It could get even worse. This is an absolute betrayal of our seniors. I came together with unions and seniors to call out these attacks and demand Trump stay away from Social Security. So I need you with me: | | On Day One of the Trump administration, Elon Musk made Social Security a #1 target for his massive budget cuts. DOGE has already set plans to cut 10% of the Social Security Administration’s workforce — and that is only the start. This is nothing more than an attempt to offer gigantic tax breaks to billionaires at the expense of hardworking Americans. We can’t let it happen. Thanks for fighting with me, K.G. * = A note from Kirsten: Friend, I am truly honored to have won reelection, and I promise to continue the critical work toward bipartisan solutions for New Yorkers as we enter this new term. While we had many victories in New York this election season, our fight to retake control of the Senate is far from over. = Thank you, Kirsten Gillibrand

body:
A note for Fox News hosts
#
On Fox News, you had Jeanine Pirro say — as though this is fraud — that they found “so many” babies, two year olds, and four year olds receiving Social Security.
I’ve got a notice for you, Jeanine Pirro: those babies get Social Security because their parents died.
That’s not a waste. That’s humanity. **That’s America**.
That’s the country that we fight for.
Those are the promises that we make to one another.
That’s what it means to be in a civilized society.
That’s not waste. **It is the best of us**.
More soon,
Alexandria

I know you’re getting quite a few political emails today, so I’ll be brief.
Midnight tonight marks an important fundraising deadline for our campaign, and we're still coming up a bit short of our goal -- we have about $4,781 left to raise. Can you use the link below to chip $3, or whatever you can, before midnight?
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lf-q2-2025**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106848418/542805380/-319689629?refcode=em-4.30.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYzhjNzYzNjQtMTEyNi1mMDExLThiM2QtNjA0NWJkZWQ4Y2NhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=3KSGVCydSek9dQdIsBmczU69oqYUygeTlpT0k9MW44w=)

body:
Last night, on the 100th day of his presidency, Donald Trump returned to the state he visited almost as much as any other during the presidential campaign.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2275%2E135344%2EGFNidZ)

Friends -
Yesterday, on the 100th night of his presidency, Donald Trump returned to the state he visited almost as much as any other during the presidential campaign.
Michigan.
His rally was like many of those before it: a lot of time airing personal grievances and painting a dark picture of our country and its people.
But why did Trump choose Michigan on a day that all of the media was paying attention? He chose it because he knows what we know: Michigan is once again the center of the political universe in the next election.
We have an open Senate seat, a gubernatorial and other statewide campaigns, and contested House races that could determine control of the chamber and more.
He did it for the news media and to energize his supporters.
And now we need to do the same.
Elissa Slotkin will be working hard to swing the swing state of Michigan back to a place Democrats win up and down the ballot.
But she needs your help to get it done.
[**Can Elissa count on you to contribute $3 directly to her re-election campaign? She will use the donations to help organize around the state and turn out the voters that helped her win even though Trump carried the state as well.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-apr25.NJ6rxh&refcode=em250430-1&t=2&akid=2275%2E135344%2EGFNidZ)

Friend, This week, Donald Trump visited my home state of Michigan to celebrate his first 100 days in office. He promoted his attacks on our communities, including by sharing a video at his rally that highlighted his administration’s illegal deportations. He held his rally in a neighboring congressional district―**the same district where we and local activists held a community town hall last week** to hold their Republican member of Congress accountable and push him to vote against a right-wing agenda that attacks Medicaid, SNAP nutrition benefits, and more. The resistance is growing and together we’re fighting back against fascism. **This Thursday May 1st is May Day―a day to celebrate workers and continue our shared struggle for workers’ rights and wages.** This is our next chance to make our voices heard and resist the anti-worker agenda of the Trump administration. [**Click here to find a May Day rally near you and sign up to attend.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYKt_PNbTZJM77xb-PM80u6p8x1lMSKsjulEVkrLYyeEJWEJPzKhc_m00EbKd-bl4PsugkJB-gGtoweEPnpi98SkTNWjZ7iNy0knnoyRK5JXmrFqjWiwjLHOcgCeA2l9DD9gIL86S-LJ0ZvXrDqYzsSWU-5XUMXfjoZB5b1XSfnjHY3uopAF3vSRXVimTAhjL5zYTiGpxHhmaApxNFjd-klTimMNFtbpX0DBQYXhMidPzFhU3ARR5CVkVVwfFPKfqH-JuZzBRnWbt-tq_B38Dag/4g3/oLLjl3mrRPmtif915D_5-w/h2/h001.RVgM2xLiyzKXsC8pmMdJomTLcaMsUEoFdNOEmvIgBV8) | [RSVP](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYKt_PNbTZJM77xb-PM80u6p8x1lMSKsjulEVkrLYyeEu2TP6avBJ6dPOuB0VynA6nu3gcZEEXDFRF2gKnlIuOHqerlJibRNVZ4kc_h8ph9ciYqI6bPZgRutIsv1djAJJtUE5c8obrZ7Li5vLtUQQlSYU-U6sPUzhi-GtWsMMsX6tot6t5exdI-K5_I73LndhIox_XAsfDpNXfPRRu5_Ungi8zXL8OqtFFqVusqtJxD-VBegLLrsmSdJkgQvYY6yvdmdQrKhJ3TzZv-66zNaRDg/4g3/oLLjl3mrRPmtif915D_5-w/h3/h001.EW0tYIXQbAHjacfaLgKDhPHB9hwUFH-NlzfpQCWWY_4)

Through these first 100 days, we have seen the power of our resistance movement.
This week, student movement leader Mohsen Mahdawi has been temporarily released from ICE custody, due in large part to our shared activism, demanding his due process rights.
At the same time, the Trump administration has restored the legal status of thousands of international students whose student visas had been revoked. This is thanks to public pressure.
The Trump administration is also consistently losing in court, losing 93% of the cases being heard. Trump and Elon Musk are also losing in the court of public opinion, with approval ratings in the negative. Their agenda is unpopular, and it’s on us to keep pushing for a future that works for working people, and all who call this country home.
[**Click here to keep up our momentum and find a May Day rally near you.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYKt_PNbTZJM77xb-PM80u6p8x1lMSKsjulEVkrLYyeEuZX7O_qMzT-dkd019hGQ_kYX-290t1zZSwszPjeA7RLjQDIBSUCMMp5dp3eBhkzs1TW1zY4ZBX49uH4zFrtbAh1ZToGJq9FLtCREC1SXTg4Ja-HXrhYZHrNDYS6h2F98v3posqcVQ-54jyX9Mnf2UEbAp57_2v-TkHgokagtZYLdrF35Jn--iowJwK5PGhgFdkKIMffFcW44xNXT86E1LmZ8XpEZTJ4U-u7oOOBIuao/4g3/oLLjl3mrRPmtif915D_5-w/h4/h001.0WA2HEEWHQfKN5kCTs2Um8-1xXIi3bnoLJmLs9GjBd8)
The coalition of grassroots groups and unions putting on May Day events explains:
> _“This is a war on working people—and we will not stand down. They’re defunding our schools, privatizing public services, attacking unions, and targeting immigrant families with fear and violence. Working people built this nation and we know how to take care of each other. We won’t back down—we will never stop fighting for our families and the rights and freedoms that propel opportunity and a better life for all Americans. Their time is up.”_
Thank you for standing with me as, together, we resist an authoritarian administration and reclaim our government for the people, not the billionaires.
With you in this fight for a better future,
Rashida

clean_body: Thank you for standing with me as, together, we resist an authoritarian administration that seeks to create a government for the billionaires, not the people. | | | Friend, This week, Donald Trump visited my home state of Michigan to celebrate his first 100 days in office. He promoted his attacks on our communities, including by sharing a video at his rally that highlighted his administration’s illegal deportations. He held his rally in a neighboring congressional district―the same district where we and local activists held a community town hall last week to hold their Republican member of Congress accountable and push him to vote against a right-wing agenda that attacks Medicaid, SNAP nutrition benefits, and more. Through Trump’s first 100 days, our communities have shown incredible strength and resilience, rallying in cities and towns in all 50 states, including outside of federal buildings like Veterans Hospitals and Social Security field offices. The resistance is growing and together we’re fighting back against fascism. This Thursday May 1st is May Day―a day to celebrate workers and continue our shared struggle for workers’ rights and wages. This is our next chance to make our voices heard and resist the anti-worker agenda of the Trump administration. | Through these first 100 days, we have seen the power of our resistance movement. This week, student movement leader Mohsen Mahdawi has been temporarily released from ICE custody, due in large part to our shared activism, demanding his due process rights. At the same time, the Trump administration has restored the legal status of thousands of international students whose student visas had been revoked. This is thanks to public pressure. The Trump administration is also consistently losing in court, losing 93% of the cases being heard. Trump and Elon Musk are also losing in the court of public opinion, with approval ratings in the negative. Their agenda is unpopular, and it’s on us to keep pushing for a future that works for working people, and all who call this country home. The coalition of grassroots groups and unions putting on May Day events explains: “This is a war on working people—and we will not stand down. They’re defunding our schools, privatizing public services, attacking unions, and targeting immigrant families with fear and violence. Working people built this nation and we know how to take care of each other. We won’t back down—we will never stop fighting for our families and the rights and freedoms that propel opportunity and a better life for all Americans. Their time is up.” Thank you for standing with me as, together, we resist an authoritarian administration and reclaim our government for the people, not the billionaires. Hi friend, I’m reaching out ahead of tonight’s end-of-month fundraising benchmark.

Here’s the truth: Asking my supporters to chip in to my campaign is my least favorite part of running for Congress – by far.

But as we prepare for the re-election fight ahead, it’s necessary. We already have two declared Republican opponents, and it’s only a matter of time before billionaires and special interest groups wade into this race.

With only three seats separating control of the House, every race matters, and as someone who defeated a self-funder to flip this seat back in 2022, I’m a clear GOP target.

Despite the noise, what remains most important to me is the thousands of Central and Southern Illinois families counting on me to deliver for them in Washington. I’m not about to let them down.

Peter,
Today in history — April 30, 1789 — George Washington stood at Federal Hall and became the first President of the United States.
He wore no crown. He took no title beyond “Mr. President.” And after two terms, he stepped aside. Voluntarily!
Because he knew: In a democracy, power is meant to pass.
Fast forward to 2025: Donald Trump has not only returned to power — he’s now teasing a third term. He’s claimed there are “methods” to make it happen. That’s not just unconstitutional. That’s un-American.
He’s not joking and we can’t take the risk.
That’s why GOTV PAC is fighting back hard in 2025. Let me leave you with something positive
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=39688%2E3422442%2E4vnOE0)
Dear Derek,
This week marks 100 days since Donald Trump was sworn into his second term.
**[Before I talk a little bit more about how I’ve been thinking about Trump’s first 100 days, will you chip in $10 before our April deadline to power my campaign for governor?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250430_2_ak?refcode=em20250430-39688&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39688_3422442_4vnOE0&akid=39688%2E3422442%2E4vnOE0)**
Here’s just a sample of what we’ve seen so far:
* Illegal deportations, including of U.S. citizen children, without due process
* Chaotic tariff policy; making it harder to do business and raising prices for families
* Threats to our health care to fund tax breaks for Trump’s ultra-wealthy cronies
* Attacks on federal workers and the role of government in lifesaving medical research, education, public health, and so much more

But, we’ve also seen everyday Americans coming together and raising their voices to stop Trump’s most harmful policies.
I know that for many of us, it’s felt a lot longer than 100 days.
And while I’m pissed off by Trump’s actions hurting and destabilizing us, I’m also hopeful—because I see so many Americans getting off the sidelines and making clear that what he’s doing is absolutely unacceptable.
This is _our_ country, and we aren’t going to let Trump and his extremist MAGA movement take it from us.
I’m running for governor to amplify the voices of California families and make life easier for them. If that means going toe to toe with the president or his allies, I have the backbone to do it.
**[Today is also the last day for us to hit our April fundraising goal. I’ve been so grateful for the outpouring of support we’ve received so far. I’m asking you one last time to donate $10 or whatever you can, so I can keep doing this work of standing up to Trump and standing up for what our families need.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250430_2_ak?refcode=em20250430-39688&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39688_3422442_4vnOE0&akid=39688%2E3422442%2E4vnOE0)**

Onward,
Katie

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

President Trump needs all the support he can get, and the Radical Left is already working tirelessly to take away our Senate Majority. If they're successful in 2026, they'll continue the endless witch-hunts and do anything they can to turn President Trump's second half into a lame-duck presidency. The American People gave President Trump and the Senate Majority a mandate on November 6, 2024. It's our duty to uphold this America-First Mandate and deliver for the American People. Now, my April fundraising deadline is TONIGHT AT MIDNIGHT. I 'M BEHIND MY FUNDRAISING GOALS!! God Bless America, Coach Tuberville Meet Coach Tuberville: Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces. In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud. In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others. In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. Now, Coach Tuberville is running for re-election so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in the United States Senate.
